The fields are certified under Yamagata Prefecture's special cultivation program, which includes cutting chemical pesticide use in half, aiming for safe, flavor-rich wine.
features_en: A domaine winery, using only its own grapes
About 9 hectares of estate vineyards at the foot of Mount Zao
Certified under Yamagata's special cultivation program

yamanashi:yawata-yosyu.tagline_en: Since 1961, farmers in Yawata have pooled their grapes at this community winery, producing a different wine every vintage.
yamanashi:yawata-yosyu.desc_en: Yawata Yoshu began in 1961 when farmers in the local Yawata district started pooling their grapes together. The winery draws out the full character of grapes whose sweetness and aroma shift with each year's climate and harvest timing, resulting in a wine that tastes a little different every year.
features_en: A community winery founded in 1961 by farmers pooling their grapes
Individualistic wine whose character changes with each vintage
Also sold at the local JA farm shop

甲州（辛口）.specs_en: White — dry, Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape)

マスカットベーリーA.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

yamanashi:kashiwa-budoushu.tagline_en: At Daizenji, Japan's only temple winery, the head priest and local parishioners pool their own grapes into small-batch wine.
yamanashi:kashiwa-budoushu.desc_en: Kashiwa Budoushu is a unique winery made by the head priest of Daizenji temple together with nearby parishioners. Grapes grown by the priest himself in the temple grounds are used alongside fruit that union members bring from their own gardens, distributed by weight, and fermented in a brewing hut on the temple grounds.
features_en: Japan's only temple-run winery, operated by Daizenji
Community winemaking using grapes brought by parishioner union members
Sold at the Daizenji temple shop

yamanashi:spring-wine.tagline_en: A new Yamanashi winery, Spring Wine began making wine in September 2024, founded by Izumi Sano after training in viticulture.
yamanashi:spring-wine.desc_en: Spring Wine is a new winery in Kofu, Yamanashi, that built its brewery in April 2024, obtained its liquor manufacturing license that July, and began making wine in September. Founder Izumi Sano went independent after growing grapes at an agricultural production corporation and training at a winery.
features_en: Uses its own estate-grown grapes
Small-scale winemaking based in Kofu
Makes Koshu, Chardonnay and other varieties

甲州.specs_en: White — dry, Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape)

マスカット・ベーリーA.specs_en: Red — dry, Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

hokkaido:otobe-winery.tagline_en: Otobe Winery farms 10 hectares in mild, long-daylight southern Hokkaido, making about 25,000 bottles a year.
hokkaido:otobe-winery.desc_en: Otobe Winery benefits from a mild climate, the long hours of daylight typical of northern Japan, and wide swings between day and night temperature during grape ripening — conditions well suited to high-quality winemaking. Its own vineyards cover 10 hectares in total, producing about 25,000 bottles a year.
features_en: 10 hectares of estate vineyards
Produces about 25,000 bottles a year
A long-established winery in Otobe, southern Hokkaido

乙部醸造ワイン 赤.specs_en: Red — medium-bodied, 100% Hokkaido grapes, Seibel 13053, Merlot and Yama Sauvignon

乙部醸造ワイン 白.specs_en: White — medium-dry, 100% Hokkaido grapes, Zarajenje, Seibel 9110 and Chardonnay

ミスタージンギスカン.specs_en: Red — paired with Jingisukan (grilled lamb), Seibel 13053 and Yama Sauvignon

nagano:aperture-farm-winery.tagline_en: Growing grapes since 2011, Aperture Farm opened its own winery in Tomi in 2022, making natural wine with wild yeast.
nagano:aperture-farm-winery.desc_en: Aperture Farm and Winery began growing grapes in 2011 and opened its own winery in Tomi in August 2022. It makes natural wine fermented with wild yeast and minimal added sulfites, taking over Kyoho vineyards from an aging farmer and experimenting with new winemaking methods.
features_en: Natural winemaking with wild yeast and minimal sulfites
Organic estate winery in Nezu, Tomi (opened 2022)
Uses Kyoho vineyards taken over from an aging farmer

Landscape.specs_en: Red — top cuvée, wild yeast, no added sulfites, Merlot-led

yamagata:oura-budo-wine.tagline_en: In Akayu, known as the birthplace of Yamagata grape-growing, Oura Budo-shu has made wine only from quality local grapes since 1939.
yamagata:oura-budo-wine.desc_en: Akayu, in Nanyo City within the Okitama Basin, is known as the birthplace of grape-growing in Yamagata and remains one of the prefecture's leading grape regions. Since its founding, Oura Budo-shu has focused solely on high-quality local grapes for its Akayu jiwain (local wine).
features_en: Founded in 1939
Located in the Akayu hot-spring district
Uses 100% locally grown grapes

hokkaido:hakodate-wine.tagline_en: Since 1973, Hakodate Wine has made both grape and fruit wine, aiming for 'Japanese wine' suited to Japanese palates.
hokkaido:hakodate-wine.desc_en: Hakodate Wine has long made full-fledged wine from grapes as well as fruit wine from the various fruits of the land. Based in Hokkaido since 1973, it aims to create 'wine of Japan' suited to Japanese tastes.
features_en: ISO 9001 certified
Also produces fruit wines
Marked its 50th anniversary in 2023

hokkaido:osa-winery.tagline_en: Run by a husband-and-wife team, OSA Winery grows, makes and sells wine start to finish, mostly white, from Otaru and Yoichi grapes.
hokkaido:osa-winery.desc_en: OSA Winery is a small operation run by a husband-and-wife team, handling everything from growing grapes to winemaking and sales. It focuses mainly on white wine, made to complement Japanese cuisine, using grapes harvested from its own vineyards in Otaru and Yoichi.
features_en: Run by a husband-and-wife team
White wine made to complement Japanese food
A shop near the Otaru Canal

OTARUVALLEY.specs_en: White — flagship blend of 8 varieties from the estate vineyard in Shiotani, Otaru

tabi.specs_en: White — Tabiji, a rare grape variety originating in Otaru

ocean.specs_en: White — Hokkaido-inspired aromas, made to pair with food

hokkaido:ebeotsu-wein.tagline_en: Planted in 2016 with 1,000 vines, Ebeotsu Wein released its first vintage, Regenbogen, in 2019.
hokkaido:ebeotsu-wein.desc_en: Ebeotsu Wein makes wine from grapes grown in Takikawa, cultivating two black and five white grape varieties. It planted 1,000 vines in 2016 and completed its first vintage, Regenbogen (German for 'rainbow'), in 2019.
features_en: Uses grapes grown in Takikawa, Sorachi
Grows two black and five white grape varieties

Regenbogen（レーゲンボーゲン）.specs_en: White — blend of seven Takikawa-grown varieties (Chardonnay, Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Zweigeltrebe)

yamagata:ringorillappa.tagline_en: Ringorillappa's 4.7-hectare orchard is entirely organic-JAS certified, producing Japan's first domestically certified organic cider through wild-yeast fermentation.
yamagata:ringorillappa.desc_en: Ringorillappa Brewery's 4.7-hectare apple orchard is entirely certified organic JAS, and it produces Japan's first domestically made organic cider and organic apple juice. Fermentation relies on wild yeast, keeping added ingredients to a minimum.
features_en: Japan's first organic-JAS-certified cider
Entire 4.7-hectare apple orchard is organic-JAS certified
Obtained its brewing license in 2024

有機シードル.specs_en: Cider — Japan's first domestically made organic-JAS certified

nagano:arcanvigne.tagline_en: A cradle winery for grape growers in Tomi City, Arcanvigne brews purchased and contract-brewed fruit while running Japan's first private wine academy.
nagano:arcanvigne.desc_en: Arcanvigne, run by the Japan Wine Agriculture Research Institute, was founded in 2019 in Tomi City as a 'cradle winery' — a receiving point for local grape growers, buying in fruit to brew its own wines or contract-brewing on their behalf. The winery also operates Japan's first private wine school, the Chikuma River Wine Academy, and is a sibling operation of Villa d'Est Winery. Its name comes from the French arc-en-ciel, meaning rainbow.
features_en: A 'cradle winery' that buys in local growers' grapes to brew its own wine or contract-brew for producers
Runs the Chikuma River Wine Academy, Japan's first private wine school
A sibling winery of Villa d'Est Winery
Its name derives from the French arc-en-ciel, meaning rainbow

メルロー ヴィラージュ.specs_en: Red — 100% Merlot from designated Tomi City growers

nagano:cantina-riezo.tagline_en: In one of Japan's 'most beautiful villages,' Cantina Riezo is a small family winery begun by a grower trained at Sainte-Neige, farming Chardonnay, Merlot and Barbera in Takayama since 2007.
nagano:cantina-riezo.desc_en: Cantina Riezo is a small, family-run winery in Takayama, a village designated one of the 'most beautiful villages in Japan.' Yasuyuki Yumoto, who trained in viticulture and winemaking at Sainte-Neige, began growing grapes in Takayama in 2007 and completed the winery in 2015.
features_en: Located in Takayama, designated one of the 'most beautiful villages in Japan'
A small, family-run winery
Grape growing began in 2007; the winery was completed in 2015

Merlot Strada Nuova.specs_en: Red — Merlot, released only in good vintages

nagano:northern-alps-vineyard.tagline_en: Below the Northern Alps in Omachi, Masaki Wakabayashi turned a childhood dream into vineyards in 2008, crafting wine like handmade artisan work.
nagano:northern-alps-vineyard.desc_en: Northern Alps Vineyard sits at the foot of the Northern Alps in Omachi. Owner Masaki Wakabayashi began growing grapes on his family's farmland in 2008 to fulfill a dream held since his twenties, and the winery was established in 2015. It aims to make wine like a craftsman's handmade work, and holds national certification as a sixth-sector-industrialization winery.
features_en: Located at the foot of the Northern Alps in Omachi
Grape growing began in 2008; the winery was established in 2015
Certified by the national government as a sixth-sector-industrialization winery

nagano:bonjour-farm.tagline_en: A physician's grape-growing hobby begun in 2008 matured into Bonjour Farm's own winery in 2021, growing Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and the rare Aligoté in Tomi City.
nagano:bonjour-farm.desc_en: Bonjour Farm was founded by physician Yasushi Minowa, who began growing grapes in Nagano in 2008 (in Tomi City from 2010). After thirteen years of viticulture, he opened the winery in 2021. The farm grows Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and the rare Aligoté variety.
features_en: Founded by a physician who turned a grape-growing hobby into a full winery business
Grape growing began in 2008; the winery opened in 2021
Grows the rare Aligoté variety

ぼんじゅーる農園 アリゴテ.specs_en: White — a rare planting of Aligoté

nagano:nishiida-sake.tagline_en: A sake brewery since the late Edo period, Nishiida also crafts Merows wine from local Niagara grapes, fermented with a flower yeast developed with Tokyo University of Agriculture.
nagano:nishiida-sake.desc_en: Nishiida Sake Brewery, founded in the late Edo period, also produces Shinshu Local Wine Merows, a handcrafted wine made from locally grown Niagara grapes. Working with Tokyo University of Agriculture, the brewery uses a yeast isolated from vinca (periwinkle) flowers to ferment the wine.
features_en: A sake brewery founded in the late Edo period
Developed a flower-yeast wine in partnership with Tokyo University of Agriculture
Uses yeast isolated from vinca (periwinkle) flowers

信州の地ワイン メローズ.specs_en: White — made with vinca flower yeast, Niagara

nagano:cyclo-vineyards.tagline_en: Former professional cyclists, the Iijima couple planted vines in Tomi City's clay-rich Yaehara district from 2014 and opened Cyclo Vineyards in 2019.
nagano:cyclo-vineyards.desc_en: Cyclo Vineyards was founded by former professional cyclist Iijima and his wife, who began growing grapes in the Yaehara district of Tomi City — part of the Chikuma River Wine Valley's eastern area, known for its strong clay soils — in 2014, completing their own winery in 2019. The company's name is French for 'bicycle.' Its wines have been selected by restaurants listed in the Michelin Guide.
features_en: Founded by a former professional cyclist; the name is French for 'bicycle'
Located in Yaehara, the Chikuma River Wine Valley's eastern district, known for strong clay soils
Wines selected by Michelin Guide-listed restaurants

パシュート シャルドネ.specs_en: White — fermented and aged in stainless steel tanks, Chardonnay

メルロー.specs_en: Red — aged 18 months in French oak, Merlot

nagano:tsuiji-lab.tagline_en: Winemaker Takahiro Suga, trained in Australia and Europe, leads Tsuiji Lab's experimental winemaking with grapes from Tomi City producers since 2020.
nagano:tsuiji-lab.desc_en: Tsuiji Lab was established in 2020 in Tomi City, bringing in winemaker Takahiro Suga, who trained in Australia and Europe, to pursue experimental winemaking using grapes from local producers. The winery, part of the Chikuma River Wine Valley's eastern district, also takes on contract brewing for area growers.
features_en: A collaborative winery led by a winemaker trained in Australia and Europe
Also contract-brews wine using grapes from local producers
Located in the Chikuma River Wine Valley's eastern district

nagano:kawashima-jozo.tagline_en: Moving to Takayama village in 2015, Kawashima Jozo farms organically and ferments with wild yeast and no added sulfites for a fully natural white.
nagano:kawashima-jozo.desc_en: Kawashima Jozo relocated to Takayama village in 2015 to begin organic (bio) grape growing, using only the permitted lime-sulfur mixture and Bordeaux mixture. Its wine is fermented with wild yeast and made without added sulfites, in a fully natural style.
features_en: Organic (bio) grape cultivation
Fully natural winemaking with wild yeast and no added sulfites
A notable new producer in Takayama village

Ou白.specs_en: White — wild yeast, no added sulfites; Semillon and Riesling

nagano:kifutato-wines.tagline_en: At 900 to 1,300 meters on the cool west flank of Yatsugatake, Kifutato Wines — named for its family's initials — became the valley's fifth winery in 2024.
nagano:kifutato-wines.desc_en: Kifutato Wines is a family farm at 900 to 1,300 meters elevation on the cool western foot of Yatsugatake, its name formed from the initials of family members. The winery was completed in 2024, becoming the fifth winery in the Yatsugatake west-foot wine valley, and harvested its first estate vintage that year.
features_en: Situated at 900-1,300 meters, an unusually high and cool elevation
The fifth winery in the Yatsugatake west-foot wine valley, opened in 2024
A family-run domaine winery

Unwind Blanc.specs_en: White — Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Pinot Gris and Pinot Blanc blend

Ohayou Geraldo Rouge.specs_en: Red — Merlot and Pinot Noir blend

nagano:sail-the-ship.tagline_en: On a small hill in Ueda's Higashiyama, Sail the Ship Winery farms Cabernet Franc without herbicides or synthetic pesticides, tending soil, insects and microbes since 2016.
nagano:sail-the-ship.desc_en: Sail the Ship Winery planted its vines on a small hill in Higashiyama, Ueda, in 2016. Grapes are farmed without herbicides or synthetic pesticides, in cultivation that values the soil, insects and microbes, with Cabernet Franc as the winery's main variety.
features_en: Natural cultivation without herbicides or synthetic pesticides
Located on a hill in Higashiyama, Ueda
A Cabernet Franc-focused winery

ケシキ.specs_en: Red — grown without herbicides or synthetic pesticides, Cabernet Franc

nagano:cave-de-mido.tagline_en: Backed by the Rue de Vin group, Cave de Mido is a cradle winery supporting Mido-district growers with mechanized viticulture, brewing know-how and sales in one operation.
nagano:cave-de-mido.desc_en: Cave de Mido was established by the Rue de Vin group as a cradle-type winery in the Nezu Mido area of Tomi City. It supports local growers with mechanized viticulture assistance, winemaking technical support and wine sales, all in one operation.
features_en: A cradle-type winery established by the Rue de Vin group
Provides growers with combined cultivation, brewing and sales support
Located in the Nezu Mido area of Tomi City

yamagata:sakai-winery.tagline_en: Tohoku's oldest winery, Sakai Winery has farmed without chemical fertilizers or pesticides since 1892, working to revive fallow fields in Akayu.
yamagata:sakai-winery.desc_en: Sakai Winery, founded in 1892 in Akayu, Nan'yo, is Tohoku's oldest winery. It farms without chemical fertilizers or pesticides, aiming for diverse plantings and a vineyard rich in wildlife, and is working to expand its fields to revive fallow land in the area.
features_en: Tohoku's oldest winery, founded in 1892
Farmed without pesticides or chemical fertilizers

yamagata:asahimachi-wine.tagline_en: Since 1944, Asahimachi Wine has paired grape farmers with winemakers under one belief — no good wine without good grapes — earning golds and a place at the 2016 G7 summit.
yamagata:asahimachi-wine.desc_en: Asahimachi Wine was founded in 1944 on the principle that there is no good wine without good grapes, bringing grape farmers and winemaking technicians together to pursue quality. The winery won consecutive gold medals at the Japan Wine Competition in 2013 and 2014, and its wine was served at the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit.
features_en: Founded in 1944
Consecutive gold medals at the Japan Wine Competition in 2013 and 2014
Wine served at the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit

yamagata:sudo-budo-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 1921, Sudo Grape Wine Factory is one of Yamagata's smallest wineries, a family running everything from Muscat Bailey A cultivation to brewing and sales.
yamagata:sudo-budo-wine.desc_en: Sudo Grape Wine Factory, maker of Nan'yo Wine, has been run as a family operation since 1921, handling everything from Muscat Bailey A grape cultivation through brewing to sales. It is one of the smallest wineries in Yamagata Prefecture, placing particular emphasis on the quality of its raw grapes.
features_en: A family-run operation, one of the smallest wineries in Yamagata Prefecture
Handles cultivation through sales in-house

hokkaido:domaine-mizuki.tagline_en: Yoichi's first grower-owned winery, Domaine Mizuki Nakai is run by fifth-generation farmer Mizuki Nakai, trained at Domaine Takahiko, crafting deep, flavorful Pinot Noir rosé.
hokkaido:domaine-mizuki.desc_en: Domaine Mizuki Nakai, founded in 2023, is Yoichi town's first winery run directly by a grape-growing family. It focuses on Pinot Noir, aiming for a deep, flavorful rosé. Mizuki Nakai, born in Yoichi in 1996, is the fifth generation of the Nakai Kanko orchard family and trained at Domaine Takahiko.
features_en: Yoichi's first grower-owned winery
Run by fifth-generation farmer Mizuki Nakai
Trained at Domaine Takahiko

hokkaido:okushiri-winery.tagline_en: Born from Okushiri Island's recovery after the 1993 earthquake, Okushiri Winery began with native wild grapevines before expanding into ten wine varieties.
hokkaido:okushiri-winery.desc_en: Okushiri Winery was established in 2007 to support the recovery of Okushiri Island following the 1993 earthquake. It began by planting seedlings of the island's native wild grape (yamabudo), before moving into full-scale cultivation of wine-specific varieties, and now grows ten grape varieties.
features_en: An island winery
A symbol of Okushiri Island's earthquake recovery
Began with native wild grapevines; now grows ten varieties

hokkaido:berry-berry-farm.tagline_en: A JAS-certified organic 50-hectare farm in Niki, Berry Berry Farm & Winery grows berries alongside Niagara, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir for its organic wines.
hokkaido:berry-berry-farm.desc_en: Berry Berry Farm & Winery Niki operates a 50-hectare farm certified organic under JAS standards and as a specially cultivated farm. Alongside blueberries and raspberries, it grows Niagara, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir grapes, which it brews into organic wine.
features_en: JAS organic-certified farm
A large-scale, 50-hectare farm
Specializes in organic wine

hokkaido:vina-de-oro-bodega.tagline_en: Started in 2018 by Japan's youngest winemaker at the time, Vina de Oro Bodega crafts Pinot Noir reds and Niagara-based sparkling wines from its own Niki-town vineyard.
hokkaido:vina-de-oro-bodega.desc_en: Vina de Oro Bodega began in 2018 with its founder's first vintage as Japan's youngest winemaker at the time. The winery's brewing centers on grapes from Niki town, including its own estate vineyard.
features_en: Founded in 2018 by Japan's youngest winemaker at the time
Uses grapes from its own vineyard in Niki town

hokkaido:sapporo-wine.tagline_en: Sapporo's fourth winery, founded in May 2020, Sapporo Wine brews Chardonnay and Yama Sauvignon from grapes grown near the city for a community-loved wine.
hokkaido:sapporo-wine.desc_en: Sapporo Wine was founded in May 2020 as the fourth winery in Sapporo city, brewing wine from grapes grown in the area around the city with the aim of making wine loved widely by the local community.
features_en: Sapporo's fourth winery
Community-oriented winemaking using grapes grown near the city

さっぽろワイン ヤマソーヴィニョン.specs_en: Red — Yama Sauvignon, a community-rooted wine

hokkaido:tokachi-makiba-winery.tagline_en: Run by the Makiba no Ie ranch in Ikeda town, this Tokachi winery grows native varieties — Yamasachi, Kiyomi, Kiyomai and Niagara — for its 2021 debut.
hokkaido:tokachi-makiba-winery.desc_en: Tokachi Makiba no Ie Winery is operated by the Makiba no Ie ranch in Ikeda town, using grapes grown in the Tokachi region. It cultivates native Tokachi varieties, including Yamasachi, Kiyomi, Kiyomai, Niagara and New Niagara.
features_en: Operated by the Makiba no Ie ranch
Grows native Tokachi grape varieties
Located within Ikeda town

hokkaido:due-punti.tagline_en: A rising Donan winery in Hokuto's Fuzuki district, DUE PUNTI Vineyards grows Merlot, Pinot Noir and Pinot Blanc and takes part in the Donan Wine Garden.
hokkaido:due-punti.desc_en: DUE PUNTI Vineyards is a new winery in the Fuzuki district of Hokuto city, in Hokkaido's Donan region, growing Merlot, Pinot Noir and Pinot Blanc. It takes an active part in local events such as the Donan Wine Garden.
features_en: Located in the Donan region of Hokuto city
Takes part in the Donan Wine Garden event
Run by an up-and-coming grower and winemaker

fukushima:wine-kobo-aizu.tagline_en: At the foot of Mt. Bandai in Inawashiro, Wine Kobo Aizu ferments and ages its wine in glass barrels, crafting a rare Aizu wine from local fruit since 1998.
fukushima:wine-kobo-aizu.desc_en: Wine Kobo Aizu is a small winery at the foot of Mt. Bandai in Inawashiro town, Fukushima. It ferments and ages its wine mainly in glass barrels, brewing a rare Aizu wine using locally grown fruit. In April 2025, the winery was transferred to the Fruit Research Institute of Showa Kako Corporation.
features_en: Located at the foot of Mt. Bandai in Inawashiro town
Ferments and ages wine mainly in glass barrels
Transferred to Showa Kako Corporation's Fruit Research Institute in April 2025

kyoto:tamba-wine.tagline_en: Kyoto's first winery, Tamba Wine has grown more than fifty grape varieties since 1979, pursuing wine that is simple yet rich enough to be one of a kind.
kyoto:tamba-wine.desc_en: Tamba Wine, founded in 1979 as Kyoto's first winery, set out to permanently produce wine that carries forward part of the city's historic food culture — modest and simple, yet rich in warmth and joy, and unlike any other in the world. The winery grows more than fifty grape varieties and operates the attached restaurant du Tamba.
features_en: Kyoto's first winery, founded in 1979
Grows more than fifty grape varieties
Restaurant du Tamba is attached to the winery

iwate:kuzumaki-wine.tagline_en: In Kuzumaki, Iwate's yamabudo country, this town-backed winery has drawn out the wild grape's bright acidity since 1986, earning honors at international competitions.
iwate:kuzumaki-wine.desc_en: Kuzumaki Wine specializes in cultivating and brewing yamabudo, Japan's native wild grape, in Kuzumaki town, Iwate — a region known for the variety. The winery, operated as a third-sector venture with the town, aims to bring out yamabudo's clean, lively acidity and wild character, and has won awards at multiple international competitions.
features_en: Located in Kuzumaki, a region known for yamabudo (native wild grape)
Operated as a third-sector venture with the town
Committed to yamabudo-focused winemaking
Winner of awards at multiple international wine competitions

okinawa:wine-kobo-raout.tagline_en: Japan's southernmost winery, Wine Kobo RAOUT grows and brews Okinawa's native Ryukyu Ganebu wild grape 100%, capturing the island's terroir in its 2023 debut.
okinawa:wine-kobo-raout.desc_en: Wine Kobo RAOUT, founded in 2023 in Onna village, is Japan's southernmost small winery. It grows and brews its wine entirely from Ryukyu Ganebu, Okinawa's native wild grape, aiming to express Okinawa's terroir directly. The winery was established by taking advantage of Onna village's special wine zone, and is Okinawa's first small winery to handle cultivation through brewing in-house.
features_en: Japan's southernmost winery, opened in 2023
Uses 100% Ryukyu Ganebu, Okinawa's native wild grape
Established under Onna village's special wine zone
Okinawa's first small winery to handle cultivation through brewing in-house

hiroshima:sera-winery.tagline_en: At 400 to 500 meters on the Sera plateau, Sera Winery brews grapes from some twenty local growers, including the Honey Venus variety, behind a glass-walled viewing corridor.
hiroshima:sera-winery.desc_en: Sera Winery sits at 400 to 500 meters elevation on the Sera plateau, brewing wine from grapes grown by about twenty farming households in the town, including the Honey Venus variety. The winery complex includes a viewing corridor over the brewing process, a restaurant and a shop.
features_en: A cool, high-elevation site on the Sera plateau
Uses grapes from about twenty growers in Sera town
A complex with a brewing-viewing corridor, restaurant and shop

hiroshima:vinoble-vineyard.tagline_en: In Miyoshi city, Vinoble Vineyard grows European varieties — Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon and Chardonnay — in a small-batch, vineyard-led estate style.
hiroshima:vinoble-vineyard.desc_en: Vinoble Vineyard grows mainly European grape varieties in Miyoshi city, Hiroshima, producing wines that showcase the character of Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc and other varieties. The estate takes a vineyard-focused approach with small-batch production of its Pinot Noir and Semillon.
features_en: Grows mainly European varieties, centered in Miyoshi city
Small-batch production of Pinot Noir and Semillon
A vineyard-focused estate winery

yamanashi:katsunuma-winery.tagline_en: Since 1937, Katsunuma Winery has devoted itself entirely to Koshu, carrying Japan's indigenous white grape onto JAL international flights and into EU export markets.
yamanashi:katsunuma-winery.desc_en: Katsunuma Winery, founded in 1937, has committed itself to a single guiding belief — 'even if just one barrel, only the best' — and has focused exclusively on Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), actively pursuing its international reputation. Its wines have been served on JAL international flights since 2007 and exported to the EU since 2008.
features_en: Focuses exclusively on the Koshu grape variety
Served on JAL international flights since 2007
Exported to the EU since 2008

yamaguchi:yamaguchi-winery.tagline_en: Part of the Nagayama Sake Brewery Group, Yamaguchi Winery set out in 1999 to build Yamaguchi into a globally recognized wine region, growing Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay and Koshu.
yamaguchi:yamaguchi-winery.desc_en: Yamaguchi Winery, the wine division of the Nagayama Sake Brewery Group, was founded in 1999 with the goal of developing Yamaguchi into a wine region recognized around the world. It brews with grapes from its own and contracted farms, working with Yamaguchi Wine Farmland on estate cultivation, and offers both its oak-aged Chateau Yamaguchi line and the more approachable Soleine series.
features_en: Founded in 1999 to develop Yamaguchi into a globally recognized wine region
Partners with Yamaguchi Wine Farmland for estate grape growing
Produces the oak-aged Chateau Yamaguchi line and the approachable Soleine series

シャトーヤマグチ カベルネソーヴィニヨン.specs_en: Red, full-bodied — oak-aged, estate-grown Cabernet Sauvignon

山口ワイン ソレイネ.specs_en: Red and white — an approachable series made with Yamaguchi-grown grapes, Muscat Bailey A and Koshu

yamanashi:domaine-q.tagline_en: Founded in 2000 in Kofu, Domaine Q grows one of Japan's largest Pinot Noir plantings and releases the country's earliest nouveau each autumn.
yamanashi:domaine-q.desc_en: Domaine Q was founded in 2000 within the city of Kofu, where it grows Pinot Noir on one of the largest scales in Japan. The winery is also known for Nouveau Nouveau, made from early-picked young Delaware grapes and released as the earliest new-vintage wine in the country. A restaurant, Bordeaux, adjoins the winery, making it a destination for both wine and food.
features_en: One of Japan's largest Pinot Noir plantings
Nouveau Nouveau, made from early-picked young Delaware, released as Japan's earliest new-vintage wine
Restaurant Bordeaux adjoins the winery for food-and-wine visits

ドメーヌ久 ピノ・ノワール.specs_en: Red — 100% Pinot Noir, one of Japan's largest plantings

ヌーヌーボー.specs_en: White — early-picked young Delaware; Japan's earliest new-vintage release

yamagata:oizumi-vines-winery.tagline_en: A fruit-farming family's winery in Tendo, OIZUMI VINES WINERY built its own crush facility in 2023 and earned GI Yamagata certification the following year.
yamagata:oizumi-vines-winery.desc_en: OIZUMI VINES WINERY, run by Fruit Farm Oizumi, is built on the belief that good wine starts with good grapes. Its name reflects an aim to walk alongside its own vines. The winery's dedicated brewing facility began operating in 2023, and in November 2024 it received GI Yamagata (Geographical Indication) certification.
features_en: Run by an orchard family with deep experience in fruit growing
GI Yamagata (Geographical Indication) certified in 2024

yamanashi:ogasawara-farm.tagline_en: An agricultural corporation at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake, Ogasawara Farm opened its winery in 2022 to make one of Japan's few 100% European pear wines.
yamanashi:ogasawara-farm.desc_en: Ogasawara Farm began farming as an agricultural corporation in 2015 and opened its winery in 2022, at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake in Hokuto. Its signature product is Poiré, a wine made from European pears grown on the farm — a rare style in Japan — alongside grape wine.
features_en: Poiré, a 100% European pear wine, a rare style in Japan
A farm winery at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake, farming since 2015
Small winery opened in 2022 in Hokuto's Takane area

小笠原ファーム 西洋梨ポワレ.specs_en: Fruit wine — 100% European pear, a rare style in Japan

iwate:hiraizumi-winery.tagline_en: A small farmer-run winery near the World Heritage site of Hiraizumi, making minimal-intervention dry wines from Campbell, Niagara and wild yamabudou grapes.
iwate:hiraizumi-winery.desc_en: Hiraizumi Winery is run by the agricultural cooperative Agri Hiraizumi under the concept of 'handcrafted wine made by farmers.' The vineyards use only organic fertilizer and minimal pesticides, and the winery avoids unnecessary intervention to let the grapes' natural character come through in a dry style.
features_en: Run by local farmers as a cooperative winery
Handcrafted, natural winemaking approach
Organic fertilizer and minimal pesticide use
Located near the World Heritage site of Hiraizumi

山ぶどう.specs_en: Red — yamabudou (Japan's wild mountain grape), dry

iwate:edelwein.tagline_en: Iwate's first winery, founded in 1962 in Hanamaki, Edelwein sources 100% of its grapes from the prefecture and hosts an annual Wine Festival each September.
iwate:edelwein.desc_en: Edelwein was founded in 1962 in Hanamaki's Osasa area as Iwate's first winery, on the belief that good wine can only come from good grapes. It works with 34 local farmers and uses 100% Iwate-grown grapes, aiming to express the region's terroir. Visitors can tour the winery and taste for free at Wine Chateau Osasa, and the winery hosts a Wine Festival every year on the third Sunday of September.
features_en: Iwate's first winery, founded in 1962
Uses 100% Iwate-grown grapes
Works with 34 local partner farmers
Annual Wine Festival held every third Sunday of September

iwate:kamegamori-winery.tagline_en: Two growers — one of apples, one of grapes — founded Kamegamori Brewery in Hanamaki's Ohasama in 2015 to make unfiltered, natural cider and wine.
iwate:kamegamori-winery.desc_en: Kamegamori Brewery was founded in 2015 by an apple grower and a grape grower in Ohasama, Hanamaki. Over 90% of its apples and grapes are self-grown, farmed without herbicides or chemical fertilizer and built up with compost. The wines are made without added sugar, added acid or filtration for a natural style.
features_en: Founded jointly by an apple grower and a grape grower
No herbicides or chemical fertilizer used
Unsugared, unacidified and unfiltered natural winemaking

yamanashi:yahagi-wine.tagline_en: An additive-free wine specialist founded in 1914 in Fuefuki, Yahagi Wine grows its grapes without herbicides to let nature's own strength shine through.
yamanashi:yahagi-wine.desc_en: Yahagi Wine, founded in 1914 in the Yahagi district of Fuefuki's Ichinomiya-cho, is a brewery specializing in additive-free wine. It grows its own grapes without herbicides, strengthening the vines' roots and building resistant fruit trees with organic fertilizer to keep pesticide use to a minimum, continuing to make honest wine that draws out nature's own power.
features_en: Practices herbicide-free, minimal-pesticide natural farming
Specializes in additive-free wine
Uses grapes grown in its own vineyard

矢作ワイン 甲州.specs_en: White — 100% Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), additive-free

矢作ワイン マスカットベリーA.specs_en: Red — 100% Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red), additive-free

yamanashi:shingen-wine.tagline_en: A one-person winery in central Kofu, Shingen Wine's owner grows Cabernet Sauvignon, Kai Noir and Koshu himself and welcomes visitors year-round, no day off.
yamanashi:shingen-wine.desc_en: Shingen Wine is a 'one-person winery' where the owner handles everything from grape growing to bottling. Cabernet Sauvignon, Kai Noir, Kai Blanc and Koshu are grown in the owner's own vineyards in Fuefuki and Hokuto, and the brewery and shop sit in central Kofu, a 15-minute walk from the station's south exit. Tours are free and open year-round, with no closing days, from 8:00 to 18:00.
features_en: A one-person winery handling growing through bottling
Easy access — a 15-minute walk from Kofu Station's south exit
Open year-round for casual tasting and direct sales

yamanashi:kawanishi-winery.tagline_en: Founded in 1918 at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake, Noumien Kawanishi Winery still hand-crafts wine by traditional methods under its Mont.8 label.
yamanashi:kawanishi-winery.desc_en: Noumien Kawanishi Winery was founded in 1918 as a small, handcrafted winery in Anayama, Nirasaki, at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake. It brews wine from quality grapes harvested in the surrounding Kyohoku region, keeping to the traditional methods it has followed since its founding. Its flagship brand, Mont.8, is named for Mt. Yatsugatake.
features_en: Founded in 1918, a historic handcrafted winery in the Kyohoku region
Mont.8 brand named for Mt. Yatsugatake
Continues traditional winemaking methods from its founding

Mont.8 赤.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

iwate:gomaibashi-winery.tagline_en: A small Morioka winery founded in 2001, Gomaibashi Winery makes about 1,000 bottles a year alongside apple wine and cider from Kitakami riverside orchards.
iwate:gomaibashi-winery.desc_en: Gomaibashi Winery was founded in 2001 in Kado, Morioka, and produces a limited run of roughly 1,000 bottles a year. Alongside an original red wine from its own vineyard, it makes Gomaibashi Apple Wine using apples sourced only from the east bank of the Kitakami River, as well as cider.
features_en: Founded in 2001 in Morioka
Apples sourced only from the Kitakami River's east bank
Also produces cider

五枚橋林檎ワイン 王林.specs_en: White (apple) — Orin apples from the Kitakami River's east bank

yamanashi:domaine-hide.tagline_en: A red-wine specialist in the Minami-Alps, Domaine Hide pursues saignée-method wines with a grape-polishing ratio rivaling daiginjo sake.
yamanashi:domaine-hide.desc_en: Domaine Hide, led by Hideo Shibuya, is a red-wine specialist pursuing what it calls 'true Japanese wine.' The winery explores the saignée method and polishes its grapes to a ratio of 50% or more — comparable to daiginjo sake — under a philosophy of brewing naturally, following the moon, amid the nature of the Minami-Alps. It received its fruit wine manufacturing license on July 31, 2015, and produces about 8,000 bottles a year.
features_en: Fruit wine manufacturing license obtained July 31, 2015
Red-wine specialist using the saignée method with a 50%+ grape-polishing ratio
Annual production of about 8,000 bottles

ラピュータ.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A-led, saignée method, flagship wine

天・地・人.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A grown in the Minami-Alps, natural farming

yamanashi:wine-labo.tagline_en: Opened in 2022 by a brewing-materials importer, Wine-Labo ferments the same grapes with different yeasts to demonstrate their effect on flavor.
yamanashi:wine-labo.desc_en: Wine-Labo was opened in 2022 by Shinwa Foods Chemical, a company that imports and sells brewing materials and machinery. The winery uses its own yeast and equipment in actual production to test and demonstrate their effects, brewing Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), Merlot and Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red). It ferments the same grapes with different yeasts to show how yeast shapes aroma and flavor, and sells 300ml mini-bottles only at its own shop.
features_en: Run by a brewing yeast and materials manufacturer as a demonstration winery
Ferments the same grapes with different yeasts to show yeast's effect on flavor
300ml mini-bottles sold only at the winery's own shop

yamagata:hamada-winery.tagline_en: A Yonezawa sake brewery since 1866, Hamada began making wine in 1957 and studied at the University of Bordeaux before launching Chateau Monsan in 1976.
yamagata:hamada-winery.desc_en: Hamada was founded as a sake brewery in 1866 in Yonezawa and began wine brewing in 1957. In 1973 it succeeded with vertical-trellis, high-density vine planting, and its winemakers went on to study winemaking technique at the University of Bordeaux before launching the Chateau Monsan brand in 1976. The winery emphasizes handcrafted wine that starts with care for the vineyard.
features_en: Founded as a sake brewery in 1866
Succeeded with vertical-trellis, high-density vine planting in 1973
Winemaking studied at the University of Bordeaux

hokkaido:maoi-distillery.tagline_en: Founded in 2006 on Hokkaido's Maoi hills, MAOI Distillery now makes wine, whisky, brandy and gin using a hybrid still imported from Scotland's Forsyths in 2022.
hokkaido:maoi-distillery.desc_en: MAOI Distillery was founded in March 2006 as a winery, and was renamed MAOI Co. in the winter of 2021. In 2022 it installed a hybrid pot still from Scotland's Forsyths, and now produces wine, whisky, brandy and craft gin. Its direct-sales shop is open weekends and holidays from 13:00 to 15:00, closed in winter from January to March.
features_en: A combined wine, whisky and brandy distillery
Hybrid still imported from Scotland's Forsyths
Located on the Maoi hills

馬追ワイン.specs_en: Red — mainly Yama Sauvignon and yamabudou grown on the Maoi hills

iwate:monnosuke-farm.tagline_en: A tiny brewery amid Hanamaki's rice fields, Monnosuke Farm was designated the city's third Craft Wine and Cider Special Zone winery in 2021.
iwate:monnosuke-farm.desc_en: Monnosuke Farm sits about five minutes by car from the Hanamaki-Minami interchange, a very small brewery set among rice paddies and houses. Named for its family's traditional business name, it grows apples and grapes to make fruit wine and cider that evoke the taste of home. It was designated the third winery under Hanamaki's Craft Wine and Cider Special Zone in 2021.
features_en: Designated the third winery under Hanamaki's Craft Wine and Cider Special Zone in 2021
Grows its own apples and grapes for fruit wine
Cider bottle-fermented for over a month

もんのすけシードル.specs_en: Cider — bottle-fermented (méthode traditionnelle) for over a month, apple

iwate:takahashi-vineyard.tagline_en: Trained at Austria's national wine school, the winemaker at Takahashi Vineyard in Ohasama pursues a wine that is 'soft yet with a core.'
iwate:takahashi-vineyard.desc_en: Takahashi Vineyard is run by a winemaker trained at Austria's national wine school, in the Ohasama area of Hanamaki. Under the idea that wine is something that arises naturally in daily life — in other words, a culture — the winery aims to capture Ohasama's climate in a wine that is soft yet retains a core of structure.
features_en: Winemaker trained at Austria's national wine school
A grape-grower's winery in Hanamaki's Ohasama area
Specializes in Riesling

hokkaido:marumegane.tagline_en: A former Tokyo wine importer, Takashi Ohno moved to Niki after training in Beaujolais and began full winemaking at Domaine Marumegane in the fall of 2023.
hokkaido:marumegane.desc_en: Domaine Marumegane was founded by Takashi Ohno, a former wine importer from Tokyo who trained in Beaujolais before settling in Niki. He began growing grapes in 2018, moved to Niki in 2019, and acquired vineyard land in neighboring Yoichi, beginning full-scale winemaking in the fall of 2023.
features_en: Founded by a former wine importer trained in Beaujolais
Grapes grown since 2018 in Niki and Yoichi

yamanashi:kanai-jozo.tagline_en: A husband-and-wife winery founded in 1962, Kanai Jozo farms 0.6 hectares under a biodynamic philosophy that wine should record the land and its people.
yamanashi:kanai-jozo.desc_en: Kanai Jozo was founded in 1962 in Yamanashi City under the belief that 'wine records the nature of the land and its people.' It is run as a family winery by a husband and wife, who farm 0.6 hectares of their own vineyard while researching low-pesticide and biodynamic methods, aiming to convey the land through wine. The shop is closed on Tuesdays and closes early whenever the wine sells out.
features_en: Founded in 1962, a husband-and-wife family winery
0.6-hectare estate vineyard researching biodynamic, low-pesticide farming
Grows Koshu, Delaware, Cabernet, Merlot and Chardonnay

yamanashi:shikishima-jozo.tagline_en: At 600 meters on the southern slopes of Shosenkyo gorge, Shikishima Jozo hand-farms 14 grape varieties without herbicides to make about 30 wines.
yamanashi:shikishima-jozo.desc_en: Shikishima Jozo sits at an elevation of 600 meters on the southern foot of the Shosenkyo gorge in Kai City. It obtained its brewing license and began production in 1985, and now makes roughly 30 wines using 100% of its own estate-grown grapes across 14 varieties, farmed without herbicides and with reduced pesticide use, relying on hand labor rather than machinery. The winery also runs vine-tree and barrel-wine ownership programs.
features_en: Manufacturing license obtained and brewing begun in 1985
100% estate-grown grapes across 14 varieties, about 30 wines made
Herbicide-free, reduced-pesticide natural farming

マウントワイン ソーヴィニヨン・ブラン.specs_en: White — Sauvignon Blanc, trellis-trained (vertical shoot positioning)

マウントワイン プティ・ヴェルド.specs_en: Red — Petit Verdot, trellis-trained (vertical shoot positioning)

yamanashi:yatsushiro-jozo.tagline_en: Designated the wine industry's sole participant in Yamanashi's Specialty Village Promotion Project, Yatsushiro Jozo brews only from grapes grown in its own Yatsushiro-cho.
yamanashi:yatsushiro-jozo.desc_en: Yatsushiro Jozo works under the philosophy that good wine comes from good grapes, and is the only winery designated under Yamanashi Prefecture's Specialty Village Promotion Project. Its own farm practices organic, natural farming, and the winery uses only grapes grown locally in Yatsushiro-cho, Fuefuki. Selling direct from the brewery keeps prices low.
features_en: The wine industry's sole designee under Yamanashi's Specialty Village Promotion Project
Uses 100% Yatsushiro-cho-grown grapes, farmed organically
Also produces rare akebi fruit wine

アケビワイン.specs_en: Fruit wine — akebi, a regional specialty

yamanashi:midaigawa-winery.tagline_en: A valve manufacturer's only winery in Minami-Alps City, Midaigawa Winery began brewing in 2022 using equipment it engineers in-house.
yamanashi:midaigawa-winery.desc_en: Midaigawa Winery is run by Miyairi Valve Manufacturing and is the only winery in Minami-Alps City. It began brewing in 2022, handling everything from grape growing to production in-house, and draws on the parent company's industrial technology to develop its own winemaking equipment.
features_en: The only winery in Minami-Alps City
Founded by a valve manufacturer entering agriculture
Fully self-sufficient, from grape growing through brewing

御勅使川 マスカット・ベーリーA.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

御勅使川 甲州 ドミ・セック.specs_en: White, demi-sec — Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape)

yamanashi:sasaichi-winery.tagline_en: A sake brewery since 1661, Sasaichi Winery has made wine under its OLIFANT label since 1953 from grapes grown in its own Otsuki vineyards.
yamanashi:sasaichi-winery.desc_en: Sasaichi is a sake brewery founded in 1661 that began making wine in 1953, under the brand name OLIFANT, using grapes from its own vineyards. It occupies a rare position as a sake brewery producing Yamanashi wine.
features_en: Sake brewery founded in 1661, wine brewing began in 1953
A rare case of a sake brewery making Yamanashi wine
OLIFANT brand expresses the terroir of the Otsuki area

オリファン マスカット・ベーリーA.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

fukushima:azuma-sanroku-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of Mt. Azuma, Fukushima City's symbol, Azuma Sanroku Winery opened in 2019 to craft wine that echoes the region's four seasons.
fukushima:azuma-sanroku-winery.desc_en: Azuma Sanroku Winery was founded in 2019 at the foot of Mt. Azuma, the symbol of Fukushima City, producing fruit wine from local grapes and Fukushima's fruit. It aims for wine that reflects the prefecture's rich seasonal character. Paid guided tours with tasting are available by reservation, and its cellar-door shop offers paid tasting from 10:00 to 16:00.
features_en: Founded in 2019 at the foot of Mt. Azuma
Uses local Fukushima grapes and fruit
Offers a custom crush service

吾妻山麓ワイン.specs_en: Red and white — a series reflecting Fukushima's fruit and seasons

miyagi:akiu-winery.tagline_en: Overlooking its own vineyard and the hot-spring town of Akiu, Akiu Winery pairs Steuben, Merlot and Chardonnay wines with Miyagi's food culture.
miyagi:akiu-winery.desc_en: Akiu Winery sits in the Akiu Onsen area, known as Sendai's 'inner retreat,' on a site overlooking its own vineyard and the hot spring town. Founded in 2015, it aims to make wine that showcases Miyagi's rich food culture, and adjoins a winery café. Tours are free, with a glass-viewing space, and tastings are available from 200 yen; the winery is open 9:30 to 17:00 and closed Tuesdays.
features_en: Located in the Akiu Onsen hot-spring resort area
Founded in 2015
Winery café attached

秋保ワイン.specs_en: Red, white and cider — a series paired with Miyagi's local ingredients

tokushima:natan-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 2021 by winemaker Namika Inoshita, Natan Winery was Tokushima Prefecture's first, built around each grape's individual character.
tokushima:natan-wine.desc_en: Natan Winery was founded in 2021 by Namika Inoshita as Tokushima Prefecture's first winery. It places importance on expressing the individuality of each grape and the character of each vintage. Wines are sold through in-store direct sales, open 9:00 to 16:30, and through its online shop.
features_en: Tokushima Prefecture's first winery, founded in 2021
Led by winemaker Namika Inoshita, focused on each grape's individuality
Releases a varied lineup including DEEPER DEEPER, Rebell and MULA

hokkaido:lowbrow-craft.tagline_en: Housed in a converted stone storehouse in Yoichi, LOWBROW CRAFT began brewing in October 2022 with the aim of easy-drinking, everyday wine.
hokkaido:lowbrow-craft.desc_en: LOWBROW CRAFT aims to make wine that is easy for beginners to pick up — an uncomplicated, everyday-drinking style. It is housed in a converted old stone storehouse in Yoichi and began brewing in October 2022.
features_en: Housed in a converted stone storehouse
Focused on easy-drinking, everyday wine
Uses the rare Tabiji grape variety

TABIJI（旅路）.specs_en: White — 100% Tabiji, a rare grape variety

Roadrunner 旅路.specs_en: White — Tabiji, a rare grape variety

yamanashi:asahi-yosyu-soleil.tagline_en: A cooperative brewhouse operating since before World War II, Asahi Yoshu grows Pinot Noir, Syrah and Albariño for wine meant to pair with Japanese food.
yamanashi:asahi-yosyu-soleil.desc_en: Asahi Yoshu is a historic brewhouse that has operated since before World War II as a farmers' cooperative winery, under its current management since 2001. Its own vineyards grow European varieties including Pinot Noir, Syrah and Albariño, made as food-pairing wine meant for the Japanese table. Its labels feature artwork by printmaker Chizuru Amemiya.
features_en: European varieties — Pinot Noir, Syrah, Albariño — grown alongside Koshu
Made with the Japanese table and food-pairing in mind
Labels feature artwork by printmaker Chizuru Amemiya

ソレイユ 甲州.specs_en: White — 100% Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), food-pairing style

旭洋酒のきろく.specs_en: White — grapes grown in Yamanashi City

hokkaido:hirakawa-winery.tagline_en: On a sun-favored south slope in western Yoichi, Hirakawa Winery bottles the character of each vineyard rather than naming its grape varieties.
hokkaido:hirakawa-winery.desc_en: Hirakawa Winery, founded in 2015, is built on the belief that the best winemaking reflects the natural environment and scenery where the grapes grow, in aroma and taste. Rather than naming its grape varieties, it focuses on expressing the distinct character of each vineyard. The winery sits on a beautiful, sun-favored south-facing slope in western Yoichi, and maintains a direct-sales shop in Hiroo, Tokyo.
features_en: Wines expressing vineyard character rather than named by grape variety
Located on a south-facing slope in western Yoichi
Direct-sales shop in Hiroo, Tokyo

hokkaido:memuro-winery.tagline_en: Born from Tokachi grape growers braving winters below -20°C, Memuro Winery's cooperative domaine won a Sakura Awards 2026 Double Gold.
hokkaido:memuro-winery.desc_en: Memuro Winery is a cooperative, domaine-style winery organized by local grape growers, born from the dream of farmers working Tokachi's harsh climate, where winter temperatures drop below -20°C. It follows a 'subtraction' approach to winemaking that aims to maximize each vineyard's character. Its wine won a Double Gold at the Sakura Awards 2026 and was selected for the Kita no High Grade Shokuhin 2026 list of premium Hokkaido foods.
features_en: A cooperative, domaine-style winery organized by local grape growers
Made in Tokachi, where winters drop below -20°C
Sakura Awards 2026 Double Gold winner
Selected for the Kita no High Grade Shokuhin 2026 list of premium Hokkaido foods

iwate:iwate-kantin-winery.tagline_en: A food-canning company built a wine works at its Iwate Town factory in 1987, launching Spur Wine the following year.
iwate:iwate-kantin-winery.desc_en: Iwate Kantin, a diversified foodstuffs manufacturer, built a wine works within its factory grounds in Iwate Town in 1987 and obtained a license to produce fruit wine. The following year, in 1988, it launched a new product called Spur Wine. The winery represents the wine division of a general food company based in Iwate Prefecture, brewing at its factory in Kawaguchi, Iwate Town.
features_en: Wine works built in 1987 at the company's Iwate Town factory
Wine division of a general foodstuffs manufacturer based in Iwate Prefecture
Brewed at the company's factory in Kawaguchi, Iwate Town

yamanashi:chateau-katsunuma.tagline_en: A fourth-generation family winery since 1877, farming Toriigahira — dubbed 'Japan's Montrachet' — for some of the country's finest terroir.
yamanashi:chateau-katsunuma.desc_en: Founded in 1877, Chateau Katsunuma is a family-run winery now in its fourth generation under the Imamura family, handling grape growing, vinification and sales in-house. Its estate vineyard sits at Toriigahira, an area sometimes called 'Japan's Montrachet' and considered one of the country's finest terroirs for wine. The winery produces a wide range spanning white, red, rosé, sparkling, no-added and non-alcohol wines, and operates the adjoining Restaurant Toriigahira. Guided factory tours are currently suspended, but the shop offers free tastings of more than ten wines, with group visits of ten or more accepted by reservation.
features_en: Founded in 1877; a family winery now in its fourth generation under the Imamura family
Self-owned vineyard at Toriigahira, dubbed 'Japan's Montrachet,' among Japan's finest terroirs for wine
Wide range from white, red, rosé and sparkling to no-added and non-alcohol wines, plus the on-site Restaurant Toriigahira

シャトー勝沼 甲州白ワイン.specs_en: White — Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape); grown, vinified and bottled in-house

シャトー勝沼 無添加ワイン.specs_en: White and red — no-added, no-sugar series; Koshu and other grapes

yamanashi:nikawa-chuo-wine.tagline_en: Since 1973, this family winery in Fuefuki has grown and vinified its own Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) into dry wines under the name Liaison, French for 'to connect.'
yamanashi:nikawa-chuo-wine.desc_en: Nikawa Chuo Wine, known by its Liaison brand, is a family-run winery in Fuefuki founded in 1973 under the philosophy of 'wine that turns the earth's blessings into inspiration.' The winery handles grape growing, harvesting and vinification in-house, focusing on dry wines made with minimal chemical use and careful temperature control. Its name, Liaison, is French for 'to bind, to connect.'
features_en: Family-run winery founded in 1973
The name Liaison is French for 'to bind, to connect'
NOVICE, first vinified in 2018, is named for that new release

NOVICE 甲州 シュール・リー.specs_en: White, dry — Koshu, sur lie method

NOVICE マスカット・ベーリーA.specs_en: Red, dry — Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red)

yamanashi:mirai-yume-winery.tagline_en: Opened in 2024, this state-of-the-art natural winery grows Koshu and the rare Yamabudou-Cabernet Sauvignon cross Yama Sauvignon, made with no added sugar or sulfites.
yamanashi:mirai-yume-winery.desc_en: Mirai Yume Winery opened in 2024 as a state-of-the-art natural winery growing and vinifying Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) and Yama Sauvignon, a rare cross between wild Yamabudou grapes and Cabernet Sauvignon. Its wines are made with no added sugar and no added sulfites.
features_en: Opened in 2024 as a state-of-the-art natural winery
Wines made with no added sugar and no added sulfites
Grows the rare cross grape Yama Sauvignon (Yamabudou × Cabernet Sauvignon)

未来夢 ヤマソービニオン.specs_en: Red — Yama Sauvignon (a Yamabudou × Cabernet Sauvignon cross)

yamanashi:enzan-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 1957 and renamed Enzan Winery in 1959, it uses only Japan's native grape varieties and 100% Yamanashi-grown fruit — no European vinifera at all.
yamanashi:enzan-wine.desc_en: Founded in 1957 as a fruit growers' cooperative, Enzan Wine was renamed Enzan Winery Co. in 1959. The winery uses only Japan's native grape varieties, growing no European vinifera, and vinifies exclusively Yamanashi-grown fruit.
features_en: Uses only Japan's native grape varieties, growing no European vinifera
100% Yamanashi-grown grapes
Repeat award winner at the Japan Wine Competition

SALZ BERG Koshu.specs_en: White, dry — Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape); stainless-tank fermented, then oak-aged; tropical aromas and minerality; 11% ABV

Enzan Rouge.specs_en: Red — made with grapes grown in Koshu City

yamanashi:nakahara-winery.tagline_en: Opened in 2019 on reclaimed fallow land, this shared Katsunuma winery hosts independent producers Domaine Oyamada, Domaine Ponkotsu and Papapuru, each making wine under its own name.
yamanashi:nakahara-winery.desc_en: Nakahara Winery is a shared brewing facility established in 2019 by the Paesana agricultural cooperative corporation as part of its project to revive fallow farmland. Several independent producers — including Domaine Oyamada, Domaine Ponkotsu and Papapuru — vinify their own wines on-site, each bringing a distinct character to the shared space.
features_en: A shared brewing facility used by several independent producers, each with its own style
Part of the Paesana agricultural cooperative's project to revive fallow farmland
Home to distinctive producers including Domaine Oyamada, Domaine Ponkotsu and Papapuru

BOW!（バウ！）.specs_en: Red — Domaine Oyamada; natural, small-batch; Syrah, Mourvèdre

まどぎわ.specs_en: Red — Domaine Ponkotsu; natural, small-batch; Muscat Bailey A

Linda（リンダ）.specs_en: White — Papapuru; ripe pear and peach concentration; Koshu

yamanashi:yamanashi-hakko.tagline_en: Founded in 1961 by 450 local farming households, this cooperative winery ages its wine in a clay-walled, timber-framed building built for a stable climate.
yamanashi:yamanashi-hakko.desc_en: Yamanashi Hakko Kogyo was founded in 1961 when 450 local farming households invested to establish this cooperative winery. Its clay-walled, timber-framed building — cool in summer and warm in winter — provides an ideal, stable environment for brewing. The winery continues to make wine rooted in local production for local consumption, with brewing tours and tastings available during the fermentation season each September and October.
features_en: Founded in 1961 as a cooperative funded by 450 local farming households
Historic clay-walled, timber-framed building keeps temperatures stable year-round
Continues a local-production-for-local-consumption approach to winemaking

ベーリーA無添加.name_en: Muscat Bailey A, No Added Sulfites
ベーリーA無添加.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A; no added sulfites

yamanashi:montanus-wine.tagline_en: A small family winery in Fuefuki's Senbeiji district since 2010, hand-crafting wine from its own vineyard under a quality-over-quantity philosophy.
yamanashi:montanus-wine.desc_en: Montanus Wine is a small, family-run winery in the Senbeiji district of Isshiwa, Fuefuki, founded in 2010. Using grapes grown in its own vineyard, the winery follows a 'quality over quantity' approach, handling nearly every step from harvest to bottling by hand.
features_en: Family-run winery making wine by hand in small batches
Uses grapes from its own vineyard, favoring quality over quantity
Expresses the terroir of Senbeiji, Isshiwa, in Fuefuki

yamanashi:aramaki-winery.tagline_en: An estate winery since 1930, Aramaki has used only its own Yamanashi-grown grapes for more than 90 years, in resonance with the surrounding mountains.
yamanashi:aramaki-winery.desc_en: Aramaki Winery was founded in 1930 in Fuefuki, using only its own estate-grown grapes across more than 90 years of winemaking. Set among the mountains of Yamanashi, the winery follows a philosophy of resonance with nature. Factory tours are not offered, but free tastings are available year-round.
features_en: Uses only its own estate-grown grapes
Founded in 1930, with more than 90 years of history
No factory tours, but free tastings offered

yamanashi:katsunuma-daihachi.tagline_en: A community cooperative winery in Katsunuma's Todoriki district since 1980, brewing Koshu white wine from local grapes for visitors who book ahead.
yamanashi:katsunuma-daihachi.desc_en: Katsunuma Daihachi Budoushu is a community cooperative winery in the Todoriki district of Katsunuma, Koshu City. A member of the Yamanashi Wine Brewers' Association, it brews mainly Koshu white wine using locally grown grapes, and offers tours and tastings by advance reservation.
features_en: Member of the Yamanashi Wine Brewers' Association, committed to local grapes
A small, community-rooted winery in Katsunuma's Todoriki district
Tours and tastings available by advance reservation

hokkaido:nobori-jozo.tagline_en: Founded in 2014 by an Akita-born winemaker who settled in Yoichi, Nobori Jozo ferments its own-grown Zweigelt with wild yeast.
hokkaido:nobori-jozo.desc_en: Nobori Jozo was founded in 2014 by 小西史明, a winemaker originally from Akita Prefecture who moved to Yoichi in 2009 and began growing grapes on his own farm in 2011. The winery ferments with wild yeast and focuses mainly on wines made from Zweigelt grapes.
features_en: Fermented with wild yeast
Grapes grown on the winery's own farm

hokkaido:tsukiura-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 2000 above Lake Toya and Mount Usu, Tsukiura Winery grows Dornfelder grapes chosen through years of trial and error.
hokkaido:tsukiura-wine.desc_en: Tsukiura Winery was founded in 2000, beginning with a vineyard planted at Tsukiura, overlooking Lake Toya and Mount Usu. Aiming to grow grapes suited to Hokkaido's climate, the winery went through repeated trial and error in soil improvement and variety selection.
features_en: Scenic vineyard overlooking Lake Toya and Mount Usu

hokkaido:hakkenzan-winery.tagline_en: Thirty minutes from central Sapporo, Hakkenzan Winery has earned international awards for its Koi Wine series since its 2016 release.
hokkaido:hakkenzan-winery.desc_en: Hakkenzan Winery, founded in 2011 about 30 minutes by car from central Sapporo, makes distinctive local wines from grapes and apples grown on its own vineyard and by neighboring farmers. Its Koi Wine series, released in 2016, has won international awards. The winery runs guided mini-tours with pickup service and operates Hakkenzan Kitchen & Marché, opened in 2020.
features_en: About 30 minutes by car from central Sapporo
Runs guided winery tours with pickup service
Hakkenzan Kitchen & Marché on-site since 2020
International competition award winner

恋ワインシリーズ.specs_en: Sweet wine — Hokkaido GI-certified, made with the winery's proprietary CuVT method; Campbell, Portland

KANONZ 赤ワイン.specs_en: Red — estate-grown European and hybrid varieties; Merlot, Seibel 13053 and others

K-Rouge#1.specs_en: Red — blend of estate-grown varieties; Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Almo Noir

hokkaido:tsurunuma-winery.tagline_en: Overlooking the Ishikari River in Urausu, Hokkaido Wine's Tsurunuma estate has grown grapes on Japan's largest vertical-trellis vineyard — 447 hectares — since 1972.
hokkaido:tsurunuma-winery.desc_en: Tsurunuma Winery, part of Hokkaido Wine Co., was founded in 1972 on a southwest-facing slope above the Ishikari River in Urausu, Kabato District. Its vineyard spans 447 hectares of vertical trellising — the largest in Japan — where the company is also trialing AI- and robot-assisted smart farming.
features_en: Japan's largest vertical-trellis vineyard, at 447 hectares
Trialing AI- and robot-assisted smart farming
Grows 40 grape varieties

hokkaido:tada-winery.tagline_en: Farming without herbicides or chemical fertilizer in the Furano basin since 2016, Tada Winery ferments with wild yeast to let its terroir speak.
hokkaido:tada-winery.desc_en: Tada Winery, founded in 2016 in Kamifurano, farms without herbicides or chemical fertilizer, drawing on the Furano basin's underground water and mineral-rich soil. Fermentation relies on wild yeast, aiming for wine that expresses the character of its land. The winery adjoins a lodge, Winery no Yado Inaka Club.
features_en: No herbicides or chemical fertilizer used
Fermented with wild yeast
Adjoining lodge, Winery no Yado Inaka Club

hokkaido:camel-farm.tagline_en: Founded in 2017 in Yoichi, Camel Farm pairs a 40-year-old Guyot-trained vineyard with Italian winemaking technology in pursuit of world-class wine.
hokkaido:camel-farm.desc_en: Camel Farm Winery was founded in 2017 in Yoichi, growing grapes on a 40-year-old Guyot-trained vineyard and vinifying with imported Italian winemaking technology, with the aim of producing world-class wine.
features_en: 16.2 hectares of vineyard in total
Italian winemaking technology
Grows 10 grape varieties

hokkaido:hokkaido-space-winery.tagline_en: Japan's first shared-brewing winery, opened in 2023 in Naganuma, lets several small wineries split costs and share technology under one roof.
hokkaido:hokkaido-space-winery.desc_en: Hokkaido SPACE Winery, founded in 2023 in Naganuma, is Japan's first shared brewing facility, where several small and mid-sized wineries coexist, splitting costs and sharing technology. It sits about 20 minutes from New Chitose Airport and 30 minutes from central Sapporo.
features_en: Japan's first shared-brewing-facility winery
Multiple wineries share the same brewing equipment
About 20 minutes from New Chitose Airport

hokkaido:domaine-ichi.tagline_en: Certified organic since its 2008 founding, Domaine ICHI made Japan's first certified organic wine in 2010 and became a certified organic winery in 2021.
hokkaido:domaine-ichi.desc_en: Domaine ICHI was founded in 2008 in Niki, growing grapes organically on its own certified organic-JAS farm. In 2010 it became the first winery in Japan to receive organic wine certification, and in 2021 it earned certification as an organic winery.
features_en: Japan's first certified organic wine, in 2010
Organic JAS certified
Certified organic winery

nagano:domaine-sourire.tagline_en: Built by a construction firm to revive fallow farmland in Shiojiri, Domaine Sourire — French for 'smile' — has grown grapes since 2013.
nagano:domaine-sourire.desc_en: Domaine Sourire was established in 2019 by Shiojiri Kenyu, a construction and food-service company, as part of a project to revive fallow farmland in Hirooka, Shiojiri. Grape growing began in 2013, ahead of the winery's 2019 opening. Sourire is French for 'smile.' The winery also runs a bakery specializing in rice-flour bread.
features_en: Part of a project to revive fallow farmland
Rice-flour specialty bakery on-site
Grape growing began in 2013, winery opened in 2019

nagano:swiss-village-winery.tagline_en: Since 1988, Swiss Village Winery has used only Nagano-grown grapes, labeling each bottle by origin, variety and vintage for full transparency.
nagano:swiss-village-winery.desc_en: Swiss Village Winery was founded in 1988 under the principle that 'wine is an agricultural product,' using only Nagano-grown grapes, mainly from Azumino. Every label states the grape's origin, variety and vintage, keeping the producer visible behind each bottle.
features_en: Labels state origin, variety and vintage for full transparency
Misato Pinot Noir has been recognized at a domestic wine competition
Several wines certified under Nagano's appellation system

三郷シャルドネ.specs_en: White — certified under Nagano's appellation system; Chardonnay

nagano:kido-winery.tagline_en: A small family winery since 2004, Kido Winery farms without herbicides and releases a rare Project K only in its very best vintages.
nagano:kido-winery.desc_en: Kido Winery was founded in 2004 by winemaker Kido, using a herbicide-free 'grass-growing' cultivation method on this small, family-run estate. Known nationwide among wine fans for its quality, the winery produces three regular series — Autumn Colors, Premium Merlot and Private Reserve — plus a top-tier Project K released only in its finest vintages.
features_en: Herbicide-free 'grass-growing' cultivation method
Small, family-run winery led by winemaker Kido
A loyal following nationwide for its high-quality wines

オータムカラーズ.specs_en: Red and white — Merlot, Chardonnay and others

nagano:nagomi-vineyards.tagline_en: Named for Kanō, the Tomi neighborhood where it has grown grapes since 2010, Nagomi Vineyards ferments with wild yeast to express its local terroir.
nagano:nagomi-vineyards.desc_en: Nagomi Vineyards takes its name from Kanō, the Tomi neighborhood where it is based — a wordplay on 'nagomi,' meaning harmony. Its founder moved to Tomi in 2010 to begin growing grapes, and the winery, established in 2018, ferments with wild yeast to make wine rooted in the local terroir.
features_en: Fermented with wild yeast
Founder moved to Tomi in 2010 to begin growing grapes
Name derived from the local place name Kanō

nagano:viniqrobe.tagline_en: The fifth winery in Takayama Village, opened in 2019, VINIQROBE pairs its Pinot Noir with one-of-a-kind labels featuring flute-accompanied dance photography.
nagano:viniqrobe.desc_en: VINIQROBE opened in September 2019 as the fifth winery in Takayama Village, having planted Pinot Noir from 2016. Each bottle carries a one-of-a-kind label featuring dance photography set to flute music.
features_en: A small estate focused on Pinot Noir
Every bottle carries a one-of-a-kind label design
The fifth winery in Takayama Village, opened in 2019

VINIQROBE ピノ・ノワール.specs_en: Red — Pinot Noir; one-of-a-kind label design

nagano:utabi-winery.tagline_en: Nagano city's first winery, completed in 2024 by a former Ritz-Carlton Tokyo sommelier, farms reclaimed fallow land at 650 meters elevation.
nagano:utabi-winery.desc_en: Utabi Winery, Nagano city's first winery, was completed in 2024 by Tanaka, a former sommelier at the Ritz-Carlton Tokyo who left the hotel industry in 2016 to make wine. The estate reclaims fallow farmland at 650 meters elevation, with maritime-influenced soil.
features_en: Nagano city's first winery, completed in 2024
Founded by a former luxury hotel sommelier
Vineyard at 650 meters elevation with maritime-influenced soil

nagano:yamabe-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of the Utsukushigahara highlands, 600 to 850 meters up, Yamabe Winery has used 100% Matsumoto-grown grapes since 2002.
nagano:yamabe-winery.desc_en: Yamabe Winery, founded in 2002, uses 100% Matsumoto-grown grapes at the foot of the Utsukushigahara highlands, between 600 and 850 meters elevation, where large day-night temperature swings and long sunshine hours favor grape growing. The winery avoids bulk wine and concentrated must, fermenting at low temperatures with hand-punched caps.
features_en: 100% Matsumoto-grown grapes
Vineyard at 600–850 meters, at the foot of the Utsukushigahara highlands
No bulk wine or concentrated must used
Low-temperature fermentation with hand-punched caps

nagano:obuse-winery.tagline_en: Founded in 1942 and now run by Burgundy-trained fourth-generation winemaker Soga, Obuse Winery pioneered pesticide-free 'Sans Chimie' wine from its own estate grapes.
nagano:obuse-winery.desc_en: Obuse Winery, founded in 1942, is now led by its fourth generation, winemaker Soga, who trained in Burgundy. Using only grapes from its own farm, the estate winery pioneered Japan's pesticide- and chemical-fertilizer-free 'Sans Chimie' wines.
features_en: Pioneer of pesticide- and chemical-fertilizer-free 'Sans Chimie' wines
Estate winery using only its own farm's grapes
Fourth-generation winemaker trained in Burgundy

ドメイヌ・ソガ プティ・マンサン モアルー.specs_en: White, sweet — Sans Chimie; Petit Manseng

yamagata:takeda-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of the Zao mountains since 1920, Takeda Winery built Japan's first successful bottle-fermented sparkling wine on a philosophy of soil-first viticulture.
yamagata:takeda-winery.desc_en: Takeda Winery has grown grapes at the foot of the Zao mountains since opening in 1920, guided by the philosophy that good wine begins with good grapes and soil-building viticulture. The winery achieved Japan's first successful bottle-fermented sparkling wine. Free guided tours run about 30 minutes and require advance reservation.
features_en: Opened in 1920
Located at the foot of the Zao mountains
Achieved Japan's first successful bottle-fermented sparkling wine

yamagata:gassan-wine.tagline_en: Run by a Shonai farmers' cooperative since 1979, Gassan Wine uses 100% locally grown grapes, with factory tours viewable through glass.
yamagata:gassan-wine.desc_en: Gassan Wine Yamabudou Laboratory is run by the Shonai Tagawa Agricultural Cooperative (JA), tracing back to 1979 when production began in the former village of Asahi. The winery uses 100% Shonai-grown grapes for its wines, with glass-viewing factory tours and free tastings.
features_en: Operated by an agricultural cooperative (JA)
Includes a dedicated Yamabudou (wild grape) research laboratory
100% Shonai-grown grapes

yamagata:gassan-toraya-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of Mount Gassan since 1982, Gassan Toraya Winery has earned gold medals at wine competitions as it refines its craft.
yamagata:gassan-toraya-winery.desc_en: Gassan Toraya Winery, founded in 1982 at the foot of Mount Gassan, makes wine from the favorable local climate and terrain. Its wines have won gold medals at wine competitions in recent years as the winery continues to refine its quality. Free tours are available by reservation, along with free tastings.
features_en: Located at the foot of Mount Gassan
Uses Yamagata-grown fruit
Also produces fruit wine and cider

hokkaido:domaine-towa.tagline_en: Run by a social welfare organization in Takasu, Domaine Towa began estate winemaking in 2024, growing seven varieties in a cool northern Hokkaido basin.
hokkaido:domaine-towa.desc_en: Domaine Towa is operated by the social welfare corporation Takasu Kyoseikai in Takasu, northern Hokkaido, growing grapes and vinifying wine on site. The winery obtained its brewing license in 2024, making it one of the region's newest producers. Seven varieties are cultivated, from Bacchus and Gewürztraminer to Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, and Zweigelt, grown in a cool basin in Japan's far north.
features_en: Operated by a social welfare corporation as an agriculture-welfare partnership winery
Grapes grown in a cool basin in Takasu, northern Hokkaido

hokkaido:10r-winery.tagline_en: Working with Hokkaido-grown grapes only, 10R Winery started as a custom-crush facility in 2012 and farms eight Dijon clones of Pinot Noir.
hokkaido:10r-winery.desc_en: 10R Winery, founded in 2009 in Iwamizawa, uses only Hokkaido-grown grapes in pursuit of high-quality wine. It began operating as a custom-crush winery (contract winemaking facility) in 2012. The estate grows eight Dijon clones of Pinot Noir, along with Gamay, Pinot Meunier, and Poulsard.
features_en: Began as a custom-crush (contract winemaking) facility
Eight Dijon clones of Pinot Noir under cultivation

hokkaido:shinga-winery.tagline_en: Near Japan's northernmost wine region, Shinga Winery in Nayoro grows Bacchus and Kojiko to express the character of the northern land.
hokkaido:shinga-winery.desc_en: Founded in 2019 in Nayoro, Hokkaido, Shinga Winery is committed to grapes grown in Nayoro, aiming to make wine that expresses the northern land. Located near Japan's northernmost wine-growing area, it grows Bacchus and Kojiko as its main varieties.
features_en: One of Japan's northernmost wineries
Focused on grapes grown in Nayoro
Kojiko and Bacchus as core varieties

hokkaido:kamui-metto-nupuri.tagline_en: Founded in 2023 beneath Hokkaido's Taisetsu range, Kamui Metto Nupuri carries an Ainu name and grows Yamasachi grapes in Kamifurano.
hokkaido:kamui-metto-nupuri.desc_en: Kamui Metto Nupuri was founded in 2023 in Kamifurano, taking its Ainu-language name as a nod to local heritage. The winery aims to make wine of the northern land, drawing on the blessings of the Taisetsu mountain range, growing Yamasachi grapes.
features_en: Winery carries an Ainu-language name
Located in Kamifurano beneath the Taisetsu mountain range

ibaraki:ushiku-chateau.tagline_en: Founded in 1903 by Denbei Kamiya, Ushiku Chateau was Japan's first full-scale winery and today operates from buildings designated Important Cultural Properties.
ibaraki:ushiku-chateau.desc_en: Ushiku Chateau traces its roots to 1903, when Denbei Kamiya opened it as the Ushiku brewery, Japan's first full-scale winery, adopting French grape varieties and Bordeaux-style winemaking techniques. Its historic building complex is now designated a National Important Cultural Property, and the winery continues to share Japanese wine culture from the same site today.
features_en: Founded in 1903 by Denbei Kamiya as the Ushiku brewery
Japan's first full-scale winery, adopting French grape varieties and Bordeaux-style winemaking
Wine-production buildings designated a National Important Cultural Property

okayama:domaine-tetta.tagline_en: At 400 meters on limestone soil in Niimi, Okayama, Domaine Tetta grows all its own grapes and began estate winemaking in 2016.
okayama:domaine-tetta.desc_en: Domaine Tetta, founded in 2009 in Tetta, Niimi City, Okayama, is a domaine-style winery using only estate-grown grapes from vineyards at 400 meters elevation on limestone soil. It began winemaking on-site in 2016, in a winery built to use a gravity-flow system. A shop and café overlook the vineyards from a terrace.

okayama:kurokamiyama-budoen.tagline_en: A small estate in Niimi, Okayama, Kurokamiyama Vineyard sends its own grapes to Shiga's Hitomi Winery for natural, unfiltered wines.
okayama:kurokamiyama-budoen.desc_en: Kurokamiyama Vineyard, founded in 2014 in Niimi, Okayama, grows its own grapes and sends them to Hitomi Winery in Shiga for contract winemaking. Grapes sent to Hitomi Winery in Shiga for contract winemaking

yamagata:yellow-magic-winery.tagline_en: Set in the Akayu hot-spring town of Nanyo, Yellow Magic Winery was founded in 2019 around a Merlot-focused vision of Japanese wine.
yamagata:yellow-magic-winery.desc_en: Yellow Magic Winery — its name translates as 'the yellow magic brewery' — was founded in 2019 in the Akayu hot-spring town of Nanyo, Yamagata. It was established around the concept of 'Japanese wine' that resonates with Asian, and especially Japanese, sensibilities: wine that makes you glad to have been born in this place. The winery focuses on Merlot.

Located in the Akayu hot-spring resort town
Focused on Merlot

yamanashi:chateau-sakaori.tagline_en: Since 1969, Chateau Sakaori in Kofu has pursued reasonably priced, high-quality wine meant for everyday enjoyment, not just special occasions.
yamanashi:chateau-sakaori.desc_en: Chateau Sakaori was founded in 1969 in Kofu with the aim of making reasonably priced, high-quality wine that can be enjoyed daily, not reserved for special occasions. Visitors can tour the winemaking facilities and underground cellar, choosing from several tasting programs, and the winery's wine was served at the G8 Ise-Shima Summit. Its lineup spans four grades — R, V, C, and SE.

Winery and underground cellar tours with multiple tasting programs

yamanashi:mars-yamanashi.tagline_en: Rooted in the region since 1960, Mars Yamanashi Winery continues Yamanashi's role as the birthplace of Japanese wine after more than 60 years of winemaking.
yamanashi:mars-yamanashi.desc_en: Mars Yamanashi Winery, founded in 1960 in Fuefuki, is a facility where visitors can see winemaking rooted in the region and its resources. It continues more than 60 years of winemaking in Yamanashi, the birthplace of Japanese wine. Grapes are sourced from five terroirs — Hozaka, Shirane, Isawa, Misaka, and Makioka — and the winery holds a cold-storage cellar for around 300,000 bottles.
