yamanashi:kinjyo-wine.tagline_en: A small hand-crafted winery in Katsunuma founded in 1939 as a growers' cooperative for their own consumption, now a Japan Winery Award honoree.

It originated when local Katsunuma grape farmers began making wine for their own consumption. The winery is a member of the Katsunuma Wineries Club and received a Japan Winery Award in 2021.

Member of the Katsunuma Wineries Club

miyazaki:kobayashi-ikoma-kogen-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 1991 on the Ikoma Plateau in Kobayashi, this winery pairs a winery tour with a restaurant and shop, known for its dialect-named 'N Damoshitan' series.
miyazaki:kobayashi-ikoma-kogen-wine.desc_en: Kobayashi Ikoma Kogen Wine, founded in 1991 on the Ikoma Plateau in Miyazaki, operates a winery tour, restaurant, and shop together within the plateau's natural setting. Custom-label bottles made to order, starting from a single bottle
A tourism-oriented winery on the Ikoma Plateau

nagano:chateau-mercian-kikyogahara.tagline_en: Housed in a building dating to 1938, Chateau Mercian's Kikyogahara Winery is the heart of Japan's premier Merlot region.
nagano:chateau-mercian-kikyogahara.desc_en: Chateau Mercian Kikyogahara Winery occupies a historic building constructed in 1938, in Kikyogahara, the birthplace of the internationally acclaimed Kikyogahara Merlot. features_en: The core winery of Kikyogahara, Japan's leading Merlot-producing area
Miniature vineyard, reception area, and barrel cellar open to visitors
Internationally acclaimed, premium Merlot

nagano:izutsu-wine.tagline_en: A Shiojiri winery since 1933, Izutsu Wine grows, ferments, and bottles 100% Shiojiri and Matsumoto-basin grapes with local contract growers.

nagano:terre-de-ciel.tagline_en: At over 800 meters in Komoro's Nukachi district, Terre de Ciel is a family winery making wine in harmony with nature on 'land in the sky.'
nagano:terre-de-ciel.desc_en: Terre de Ciel was founded in 2015 in the Nukachi district of Komoro, at an elevation above 800 meters. Local-born Takeo Ikeda and his family practice winemaking in harmony with nature on what they call 'land in the sky' — the meaning behind the name Terre de Ciel.

nagano:domaine-hiroki.tagline_en: Ikeda's first winery, opened in 2020 by a veteran grape grower, makes wine shaped by wide day-night temperature swings beneath the Northern Alps.
nagano:domaine-hiroki.desc_en: Domaine Hiroki, founded in 2020, is the first winery in Ikeda, a town in northern Azumino with views of the Northern Alps. It was realized by a viticulture professional and makes high-quality wine shaped by the area's wide swings between day and night temperatures. Vineyards sit at roughly 500 meters elevation.

nagano:il-fait-beau.tagline_en: Chikuma's first winery, Il fait beau — French for 'the weather is nice' — was founded in 2022 to reclaim abandoned farmland and reveal local terroir.
nagano:il-fait-beau.desc_en: Il fait beau, founded in 2022 in Chikuma, Nagano, is the city's first winery. It was established to help reclaim abandoned farmland and discover the area's terroir; its name is French for 'the weather is nice.' The winery grows Malbec as its signature variety for Chikuma.

Reclaiming abandoned farmland to help revitalize the local area

nagano:domaine-nakajima.tagline_en: A family-run natural winery in Tomi, Nagano, Domaine Nakajima farms steep slopes almost entirely by hand without pesticides or chemical fertilizer.
nagano:domaine-nakajima.desc_en: Domaine Nakajima, founded in 2014 in Tomi, Nagano, is a family-run natural winery that uses no pesticides or chemical fertilizers, fermenting with wild yeast and leaving wines unfiltered and unfined. Vineyards on steep slopes are farmed almost entirely by hand, and local varieties such as Kyoho and Delaware are also used.

Steep-slope vineyards farmed almost entirely by hand

nagano:yamato-grape-wine-azusagawa.tagline_en: A long-established winery in Azusagawa, Matsumoto since 1937, Yamato Grape Wine pursues world-class quality with a distinctly Japanese sense of place.
nagano:yamato-grape-wine-azusagawa.desc_en: Yamato Grape Wine's Azusagawa Winery, founded in 1937 in Azusagawa, Matsumoto City, Nagano, is a long-established producer aiming for world-class winemaking while shaping a distinctly Japanese sense of place. nara:kitani-wine.tagline_en: Nara's only winery, Kitani Wine set out to vinify Nara-grown grapes in Nara itself, with a pure, wild-yeast, unfiltered style.
nara:kitani-wine.desc_en: Kitani Wine, founded in 2018, is Nara Prefecture's only winery, established with the goal of making wine from Nara-grown grapes in Nara. Vineyards use cover-crop cultivation without herbicides, with reduced pesticides and no chemical fertilizer.

tokyo:kiyosumi-fujimaru.tagline_en: Opened in 2015 in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, this urban winery vinifies grapes from across Japan in Tokyo, connecting producers to drinkers under the banner 'wine for every day.'
tokyo:kiyosumi-fujimaru.desc_en: Kiyosumi Fujimaru Jozo, opened in June 2015 in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo, is an urban winery that vinifies grapes sourced from across Japan. tottori:daisen-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of Mount Daisen, this estate winery grows European varieties on a Hoki highland to make cool-climate white and red.
tottori:daisen-winery.desc_en: Daisen Winery is an estate winery at the foot of Mount Daisen, growing European varieties on its own highland vineyards in Hoki. It draws on the cool climate of the San'in region to make both white and red wine, with 6.5 hectares of estate vineyard planted mainly to Chardonnay and Merlot, and a target of expanding to 10 hectares by 2025.
features_en: 6.5 hectares of estate vineyard, planted mainly to Chardonnay, Merlot, and other European varieties
Target of expanding to 10 hectares by 2025

DAISEN WINERY Chardonnay.specs_en: White — estate-grown Chardonnay, the winery's flagship white

DAISEN WINERY Merlot.specs_en: Red — Merlot, reflecting the cool air at the foot of Mount Daisen

wakayama:wakayama-winery.tagline_en: Wakayama Prefecture's first winery bottles its estate-grown European varieties unfiltered and unheated, fermented with natural yeast.
wakayama:wakayama-winery.desc_en: Wakayama Winery, founded in 2015, is Wakayama Prefecture's first winery. It grows European varieties — including Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Merlot, and Cabernet Franc — across roughly one hectare of its own vineyards in Aridagawa and Arida, farmed with reduced pesticide use, and bottles its wine fermented with natural yeast, unfiltered and unheated.
features_en: Wakayama Prefecture's first winery, founded in 2015
Roughly one hectare of estate vineyard across Aridagawa and Arida
Bottled with natural yeast, unfiltered and unheated
Reduced-pesticide viticulture

TOA200.specs_en: Red/white — the winery's flagship series, built on its estate-grown grapes

yamanashi:nikkawa-winery.tagline_en: Nikkawa Winery, founded in 2020, aims to make grape growers and winemakers visible to drinkers through close ties with contract farmers.
yamanashi:nikkawa-winery.desc_en: Nikkawa Winery, a new winery founded in 2020 in Katsunuma, Koshu, aims to be a place where the faces of both grower and winemaker are visible, built on close relationships with its contract growers. Under GI Yamanashi (Geographical Indication), it makes a dry Koshu — Japan's indigenous white grape — alongside a dry red from the Bijou Noir grape.
features_en: New winery founded in 2020
Emphasizes close ties between growers and the winemaker
Closed Thursdays; tastings available

chiba:saito-budoen.tagline_en: A prewar vineyard in Yokoshibahikari, now run by its fourth generation, keeps pesticide and herbicide use to a minimum.
chiba:saito-budoen.desc_en: Saito Vineyard is a long-established grape grower in Yokoshibahikari dating to around 1930, before the war, and now run by its fourth generation. Farming with minimal pesticide and herbicide use, it makes wine that draws on Chiba's fruit character, working with Delaware and Yamabudo (Japan's wild mountain grape).
features_en: Long-established grower, founded around 1930, making wine since before the war
Now run by the fourth generation
Minimal pesticide and herbicide use

齊藤ぶどう園 ヤマブドウ.specs_en: Red — Yamabudo, Japan's wild mountain grape

osaka:katashimo-winery.tagline_en: One of western Japan's oldest wineries, Katashimo has protected Kashiwara's vineyards since 1914, applying sake fermentation know-how to Osaka wine.
osaka:katashimo-winery.desc_en: Katashimo Winery, founded in 1914, is one of the oldest wineries in western Japan. It has preserved the vineyards of Kashiwara while applying fermentation techniques drawn from sake brewing to make distinctive Osaka wine, under GI Osaka (Geographical Indication). Its estate farms with reduced pesticides and organic-centered fertilizer, and the winery also produces spirits and grappa.
features_en: One of the oldest wineries in western Japan, founded in 1914
Estate vineyard farmed with reduced pesticides and organic-centered fertilizer
Also produces spirits and grappa

柏原ワイン.specs_en: Red/white — the winery's locally rooted standard label

aomori:hachinohe-winery.tagline_en: A small, community-rooted winery in Hachinohe's Nango district growing wild yamabudou and Campbell Early grapes amid the surrounding countryside.
aomori:hachinohe-winery.desc_en: Hachinohe Winery is a small, community-rooted operation growing grapes and making wine amid the natural surroundings of Nango, in the city of Hachinohe. It works with yamabudou, Japan's native wild grape, alongside the hybrid Campbell Early.
features_en: A small winery rooted in Hachinohe's Nango district

hiroshima:fukuyama-wine-kobo.tagline_en: Run by a husband-and-wife team in Fukuyama, this winery focuses on sparkling wine from its own small vineyard.
hiroshima:fukuyama-wine-kobo.desc_en: Fukuyama Wine Kobo is run by a husband-and-wife team focused on sparkling wine, working from roughly 0.7 hectares of estate vineyard and producing about 13,000 bottles a year. The winery offers tastings by reservation and pours from a wine bar open Wednesday through Saturday evenings, a short walk from JR Fukuyama Station. Staff can also assist in French.
features_en: About 0.7 hectares of estate vineyard
Roughly 13,000 bottles produced per year
Focused primarily on sparkling wine
French-language service available
A 10-minute walk from JR Fukuyama Station

hiroshima:hiroshima-miyoshi-winery.tagline_en: In the fog-prone Miyoshi basin, this Hiroshima winery turns Pione grapes into wine, its mists sometimes yielding noble-rot fruit.
hiroshima:hiroshima-miyoshi-winery.desc_en: Hiroshima Miyoshi Winery draws on the fog that regularly settles over the Miyoshi basin, an environment that can also yield noble-rot grapes, in careful winemaking built around Pione, a table grape used here for wine. The winery produces about 260,000 bottles a year and has won numerous awards at competitions in Japan and abroad. A shop, free and paid tastings, a café, and a barbecue garden are on site.
features_en: About 260,000 bottles produced annually
Fog over the Miyoshi basin can yield noble-rot grapes
Numerous awards at competitions in Japan and abroad
Café Vine and a barbecue garden on site

hokkaido:chitose-winery.tagline_en: Grown in Chitose's cool northern climate, Kita Wine began as Yamanashi's Chuo Budoshu outpost before becoming an independent Hokkaido winery.
hokkaido:chitose-winery.desc_en: Hokkaido Chuo Budoshu's Chitose Winery makes wine shaped by the cool northern climate of GI Hokkaido (Geographical Indication). It began as the Hokkaido outpost of Yamanashi's Chuo Budoshu and became an independent company in 2011, working with grapes from contracted growers including Kimura Farm. Its Kerner, Pinot Noir, and a late-harvest Kerner make up the Kita Wine line.
features_en: Founded as the Hokkaido outpost of Yamanashi's Chuo Budoshu
Became an independent company in 2011
Grapes sourced under contract with Kimura Farm

hokkaido:boss-agri-winery.tagline_en: A family-run winery in Hokkaido's Okhotsk area, working toward 100% estate-grown fruit from cold-hardy grapes like Yamasachi.
hokkaido:boss-agri-winery.desc_en: Boss Agri Winery was established in Kitami in 2020, in Hokkaido's Okhotsk area. A family-run operation, it is working toward using 100% of its own estate-grown fruit, drawing on cold-hardy varieties such as Yamasachi alongside Chardonnay and Kerner.
features_en: Located in the Okhotsk area of Kitami
Family-run winery working toward 100% estate-grown fruit
Uses cold-hardy varieties such as Yamasachi

桜夢雫 山幸.specs_en: Red — estate-grown Yamasachi from Tanno, Kitami

nagano:kusunoki-winery.tagline_en: Using low-input, cover-cropped viticulture, this Suzaka winery pursues elegant, food-friendly wines built for the Japanese table.
nagano:kusunoki-winery.desc_en: Kusunoki Winery pursues wine that is high-quality yet gentle and elegant, made to pair with Japanese cuisine, using grapes grown under a cover-cropped regime that limits pesticides and chemical fertilizer. The owner, who studied winemaking in Australia, obtained a brewing license in 2011.
features_en: Cover-cropped viticulture with reduced pesticide and fertilizer use
Owner trained in winemaking in Australia
Obtained its winemaking license in 2011

日滝原.specs_en: White — Semillon, Sauvignon Blanc; pairs well with sashimi and sushi

nagano:shinano-wine.tagline_en: Built by three generations of father and son, Shinano Wine has long stood among Kikyogahara's leading producers.
nagano:shinano-wine.desc_en: Founded in 1916, Shinano Wine has built its reputation across three generations of father and son, becoming one of the leading wineries in Kikyogahara. Its range spans everyday-priced bottlings to premium wines, made from Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Niagara, and Chardonnay.
features_en: Founded in 1916
Built across three generations of father and son as a leading Kikyogahara winery
Lineup spans everyday-priced to premium bottlings

nagano:yamato-grape-wine-shiga.tagline_en: A century-old winery near Matsumoto, Yamato Grape Wine's Shiga winery aims for world-class quality and a distinct Japanese wine region.
nagano:yamato-grape-wine-shiga.desc_en: Yamato Grape Wine's Shiga winery is a century-old producer working toward world-class quality and a distinct Japanese wine region. Its Hagii Wine brand, renamed in 2012, blends Merlot and Chardonnay among other grapes into red and sparkling wines, and has won at Japan's domestic wine competition for four consecutive years.
features_en: A century-old winery
Renamed its "Hagii Wine" brand in 2012
Winner at Japan's domestic wine competition four years running

ハギーワイン.specs_en: Red and sparkling — Merlot, Chardonnay, and other varieties; renamed in 2012

nagano:mashino-wine.tagline_en: Rooted in the fruit-growing tradition of the Ina Valley, this winery makes an inventive, wide-ranging lineup built around Yamabudou.
nagano:mashino-wine.desc_en: Shinshu Mashino Wine grew out of the fruit-growing tradition of the Ina Valley, developing from an apple-processing cooperative founded in 1987 into a winery known for an inventive, wide-ranging lineup. Its wines draw on Yamabudou, Japan's native wild grape, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay, and Shinano Riesling, a Japan-bred variety, alongside apples and other local fruit.
features_en: Rooted in the Ina Valley's fruit-growing tradition
Developed from an apple-processing cooperative founded in 1987
Diverse products using Yamabudou, apples, and more

信濃リースリング.specs_en: White — Shinano Riesling, a Japan-bred variety

nagano:levans-vivants.tagline_en: Cultivating Gamay and Chenin Blanc alongside Pinot Noir, Les Vins Vivants draws out grape potential through vineyard-first winemaking in Tomi.
nagano:levans-vivants.desc_en: Les Vins Vivants makes wine that draws out the grapes' own potential through vineyard-focused growing. Takahiro Ogino relocated to Tomi in 2015 to begin growing grapes, and Ozamis World Co. established the winery in 2019. Alongside Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, it grows Gamay and Chenin Blanc.
features_en: Takahiro Ogino relocated to Tomi in 2015 to begin growing grapes
Ozamis World Co. established the winery in 2019
Grows Gamay and Chenin Blanc

nagano:suntory-shiojiri.tagline_en: Suntory's Shiojiri Winery keeps experimenting with brewing and aging methods, drawing on Shinshu's climate and soils for quality wine.
nagano:suntory-shiojiri.desc_en: Suntory's Shiojiri Winery, established in 1936, continues to experiment with a range of brewing and aging methods, drawing on Shinshu's climate and soils for high-quality wine. It offers Chardonnay and Merlot bottlings made from 100% Nagano-grown fruit.
features_en: Established in 1936
High-quality winemaking shaped by Shinshu's climate and soils
Chardonnay and Merlot bottlings made from 100% Nagano-grown fruit

nagano:votano-wine.tagline_en: Votano Wine grows grapes on stony vineyards along the Narai River, working to define a distinct terroir it calls Seba.
nagano:votano-wine.desc_en: Votano Wine grows wine grapes on stony vineyards along the Narai River. Its owner relocated from Tokyo and chose the site after geological survey, aiming to establish 'Seba' as a recognized terroir. The winery released its first estate-made wine in 2012, including a Seba Rosso blend of Merlot and Syrah.
features_en: Owner relocated from Tokyo and chose the site after geological survey
Working to establish 'Seba' as a recognized terroir
Released its first estate-made wine in 2012

nagano:takayashiro-farm.tagline_en: At about 400 meters on the southern slopes of Mt. Kosha, Takayashiro Farm favors quality over quantity in its winemaking.
nagano:takayashiro-farm.desc_en: Takayashiro Farm was founded by four local farming families and puts quality ahead of quantity in its winemaking. Its estate vineyard sits at roughly 400 meters on the southern foot of Mt. Kosha. Alongside wine, it produces cider, apple juice, and jam.
features_en: Founded by four local farming families
Estate vineyard at about 400 meters on Mt. Kosha's southern foot
Also produces cider, apple juice, and jam

たかやしろ シャルドネ・スパークリング.specs_en: Sparkling — Chardonnay; bronze medal at Japan Wine Competition

nagano:alps-wine.tagline_en: Backed by a cooperative of roughly 400 local grower households, Alps Wine blends producer passion with modern technology.
nagano:alps-wine.desc_en: Alps Wine was founded in 1927 and now produces about 3 million bottles a year, among the largest volumes in Japan, working with a cooperative of roughly 400 local grower households. Since 2008 it has also grown grapes through its own agricultural corporation. Its wines are made from grapes including Chardonnay, Merlot, and the Japanese variety Ryugan ('dragon's eye'), sold under labels such as Musée du Vin and Azusa Wine.
features_en: Founded in 1927
Cooperative of roughly 400 local grower households
About 3 million bottles produced annually, among Japan's largest
Growing its own grapes through an agricultural corporation since 2008

ミュゼドゥヴァン 塩尻ピノブラン.name_en: Musée du Vin Shiojiri Pinot Blanc

ミュゼドゥヴァン 善光寺竜眼.specs_en: White — Ryugan, a Japanese grape variety

nagano:ruedevin.tagline_en: Reclaiming 3.7 hectares of former apple orchard, Rue de Vin makes wine meant to revive the land and food culture.
nagano:ruedevin.desc_en: Rue de Vin was founded in 2010 on 3.7 hectares reclaimed from a former apple orchard, with a mission to draw out the land's potential while contributing to regional revival and a richer food culture. It is one of the leading wineries in the Chikuma River Wine Valley, making wines such as the dry red Deux Robes Violettes and the Chardonnay Colline d'Or.
features_en: Reclaimed 3.7 hectares of former apple orchard
Aims to draw out the land's potential and contribute to regional revival
A leading winery in the Chikuma River Wine Valley

nagano:shinshu-takayama-winery.tagline_en: Grown from Takayama Village's grape research group, this winery aims to bring the village's terroir to the world.
nagano:shinshu-takayama-winery.desc_en: Shinshu Takayama Winery grew out of the Takayama Village Wine Grape Study Group, established in 2015 with its first vintage crushed the following year. It aims to express the terroir of Takayama Village for the world, through varietal wines from Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, and Cabernet Sauvignon alongside its Murayori Family Reserve line.
features_en: Grew out of the Takayama Village Wine Grape Study Group
Established in 2015, with its first vintage crushed in 2016
Aims to express the terroir of Takayama Village

nagano:domaine-kosei.tagline_en: Specializing solely in Merlot, Domaine Kosei trains about 8 hectares of vertical shoot-positioned vines at 700 meters in Kataoka.
nagano:domaine-kosei.desc_en: Domaine Kosei is dedicated solely to Merlot, growing it on about 8 hectares of vertical shoot-positioned vines at roughly 700 meters in Shiojiri's Kataoka district. Planting began in 2016 and the winery was established in 2019, producing single-vineyard reds from Kikyogahara and Shiojiri as well as a French oak-aged bottling and a rosé.
features_en: Specializes solely in Merlot
About 8 hectares of vertical shoot-positioned vines at 700 meters in Kataoka
Planting began in 2016; winery established in 2019

片丘メルロ フレンチオーク.specs_en: Red — Merlot, aged in French oak

nagano:villadest.tagline_en: Born from an essayist-painter's 1991 move to Tomi, Villa d'Est champions satoyama living and helped pioneer the Nagano Wine movement.
nagano:villadest.desc_en: Villa d'Est Winery grew from a farm opened in 1991 when essayist and painter Toyoo Tamamura relocated to Tomi, and the winery itself was established in 2003. A pioneer of the Nagano Wine movement, it promotes the appeal of satoyama living alongside wine, producing Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc whites and a Merlot red under its Vignerons Reserve label.
features_en: Grew from a farm opened by essayist and painter Toyoo Tamamura in 1991
Winery established in 2003
A pioneer of the Nagano Wine movement

nagano:hasumi-farm.tagline_en: Once called Japan's smallest winery, this Tomi vineyard treats winemaking as an extension of its farm work.
nagano:hasumi-farm.desc_en: Now Noranorah Farm & Winery, formerly known as Hasumi Farm, treats winemaking as an extension of its farm work. Yoshiaki Hasumi relocated to Tomi and began clearing land in 2005, and the winery has been called 'Japan's smallest winery.' It operates under Tomi's special wine zone system, producing Chardonnay, Merlot, and Pinot Noir.
features_en: Called 'Japan's smallest winery'
Yoshiaki Hasumi relocated to Tomi and began clearing land in 2005
Operates under Tomi's special wine zone system

nagano:geo-hills-winery.tagline_en: Growing since 2002 under a hot spring inn's fifth-generation owner, Geo Hills Winery sits atop a windswept hill above Komoro.
nagano:geo-hills-winery.desc_en: Geo Hills Winery sits atop a windswept, breezy hill in Komoro. The fifth-generation proprietor of a local hot spring inn began growing grapes here in 2002, and the winery itself was established in 2018, working with Chardonnay, Merlot, and Gewürztraminer.
features_en: Fifth-generation hot spring inn proprietor began growing grapes in 2002
Own winery established in 2018
A breezy terroir atop the hill

トアイ・マイ・ブラン.name_en: トアイ・マイ・ブラン

niigata:echigo-winery.tagline_en: In snow country at Minamiuonuma, Echigo Winery commits to Niigata-grown grapes matured in yukimuro snow cellars.
niigata:echigo-winery.desc_en: Echigo Winery, in the snow country of Minamiuonuma, is committed to Niigata-grown grapes, aging its wines in yukimuro snow cellars. Founded in 1975, it makes Merlot and Chardonnay bottlings alongside a 雪季 (snow season) series, and operates the on-site Restaurant Budo no Hana.
features_en: Founded in 1975
Wines aged in yukimuro snow cellars
Restaurant Budo no Hana on site

越後メルロー.specs_en: Red — Merlot; awarded at the Japan Wine Competition

越後シャルドネ.specs_en: White, snow-cellar aged — Chardonnay; the winery's standard white

雪季.specs_en: Red and white, snow-cellar aged series

shimane:okuizumo-budoen.tagline_en: In the mountains along the Hiroshima border, Okuizumo Vineyard makes wine shaped by its own soil, water, and air.
shimane:okuizumo-budoen.desc_en: Okuizumo Vineyard, in the mountains along the Hiroshima border, aims to make wine that could only come from this particular soil, water, and air, in harmony with the surrounding nature. Founded in 2007, it grows Chardonnay alongside the Japanese variety 小公子, and hosts an annual harvest event at its garden café and shop.
features_en: Located in the mountains along the Hiroshima border
Winemaking aimed at harmony with nature
Hosts an annual harvest event
Garden café and shop on site

yamanashi:chateau-mercian.tagline_en: At the heart of Katsunuma, birthplace of Japanese wine, this Chateau Mercian winery pairs Koshu with international grape varieties.
yamanashi:chateau-mercian.desc_en: Chateau Mercian's Katsunuma Winery is the founding, core winery of the Chateau Mercian brand, in Katsunuma — the birthplace of Japanese wine. Its Iwamurai Vineyard grows more than 20 grape varieties, from Koshu to Merlot and Chardonnay, and the site includes a Wine Museum recognized in 2020 as a National Tangible Cultural Property marking 140 years of Japanese wine history.
features_en: Core winery of Katsunuma, the birthplace of Japanese wine
Wine Museum recognized as a National Tangible Cultural Property
More than 20 grape varieties at Iwamurai Vineyard

yamanashi:charmant-wine.tagline_en: In the cool climate of Hakushu, Charmant Wine handles everything from grape growing to aging, focused on European varieties.
yamanashi:charmant-wine.desc_en: Charmant Wine handles everything from grape growing to aging in the cool climate of Hakushu, in Hokuto. Founded in 1964, it focuses on European varieties, producing Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc.
features_en: Handles everything from grape growing to aging
Cool-climate site in Hakushu, Hokuto
Focused on European grape varieties

yamanashi:haramo-wine.tagline_en: Tucked among grape trellises in Katsunuma, Haramo Wine is a small, long-running winery pouring Koshu and Muscat Bailey A.
yamanashi:haramo-wine.desc_en: Founded in 1924, Haramo Wine is a small winery set among grape trellises in Katsunuma. It offers affordable paid tastings and makes Koshu-based white wine alongside red and rosé bottlings.
features_en: Founded in 1924
A small winery set among grape trellises
Affordable paid tastings
